Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Kibble-Zurek mechanism in the open quantum Rabi model
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: T. Pirozzi, G. Di Bello, A. Nocera, V. Cataudella, C. A. Perroni, G. De Filippis
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism provides a universal framework for predicting defect formation in non-equilibrium phase transitions. While Markovian dissipation typically degrades universal scaling, the impact of non-Markovian memory remains largely unexplored. We demonstrate that an Ohmic bath induces a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the open quantum Rabi model. Using simulations based on Matrix Product States, we show that the excitation energy strictly follows universal Kibble-Zurek power-law scaling when evaluated at the freeze-out time. Crucially, we find that since the environment defines the universality class, dissipation does not inherently compete with adiabatic dynamics, in stark contrast to Markovian regimes. Our results establish the KibbleZurek mechanism as a robust witness of universality in open quantum systems, revealing that non-Markovian memory preserves the integrity of non-equilibrium scaling. Finally, we outline a feasible protocol to simulate these non-equilibrium dynamics on gate-based quantum hardware.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Lower Bound of Thermal Conductivity in Graphene
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Yan Gao, Yafei Ding, Hongbin Xu, Zhaoxuan Tang, Fuqing Duan, Wenmei Luo, Zhensheng Zhang, Xiaohang Zhang, Guimei Zhu, Yahui Xue, Baowen Li
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: The intrinsic thermal conductivity ($κ$) of graphene remains highly controversial because of physical and metrological complexities. Although the thermal bridge method enables reliable measurements, sample fabrication remains challenging. Here, we develop a highly efficient patterning and transfer technique to systematically fabricate and characterize suspended bilayer graphene (BLG) thermal bridges with lengths of 1-30 $μ$m. Suspended BLG with unavoidable polymer residues exhibits length-independent thermal conductivity of approximately 570 W/(m K) at room temperature, remaining nearly constant from 250 to 350 K and robust to rigorous surface cleaning and amorphous silicon nitride substrates. Homogeneous non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) simulations show that amorphous carbon coverage of only approximately 0.01 monolayer is sufficient to suppress out-of-plane flexural acoustic (ZA) phonons. These findings challenge the prevailing view that rigid substrates suppress ZA phonons more strongly than surface contamination and identify a robust lower bound of $κ$ governed by amorphous surface scattering. This lower bound reflects heat conduction in graphene under realistic device conditions and provides a reference for fundamental phonon transport studies and the integration of graphene into thermal management applications in electronic devices and chips.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Observation of an anomaly in the statistics of Kibble-Zurek defects
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Jan Balewski, Alexey Khudorozhkov, Siva Darbha, Omar A. Ashour, Fangli Liu, Ermal Rrapaj, Sheng-Tao Wang, Pedro L. S. Lopes, Katherine Klymko, Milan Kornjača, Daan Camps
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism quantifies defect formation during finite-rate passage across a continuous phase transition, providing key insights into universality in quantum many-body systems. We explore counting statistics of defects in finite-rate ramp experiments on long 1D Rydberg atom chains. The experiments reveal an anomaly in the defect number distribution at long ramp times, challenging the hypothesis of defect formation through independent domain mergers. Numerical simulations reproduce the anomaly and support an interpretation in terms of post-critical coarsening during the ramp, while prepare-and-hold experiments reveal no subsequent secular growth of the measured correlations. Our results show the limits of classical or integrable system descriptions of Kibble-Zurek defect formation for interacting quantum systems.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Density-wave order enhances the phonon thermal Hall effect in a trilayer nickelate
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Qiaochao Xiang, Enkang Zhang, Xiaokang Li, Xiaodong Guo, Mengfei Zhu, Jun Zhao, Guang-Ming Zhang, Liang Li, Zengwei Zhu
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: Ruddlesden–Popper nickelates have emerged as a promising platform for high-temperature superconductivity, yet the role of lattice degrees of freedom in their correlated normal state remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the observation of a finite phonon thermal Hall effect in the trilayer nickelate La 4 Ni 3 O 10 at ambient pressure. Remarkably, the thermal Hall response is strongly enhanced below the density-wave transition at T * ≈ 140 K, exhibiting two distinct plateaus in the thermal Hall resistivity, suggesting a strong coupling between density-wave order and lattice excitations. Based on the band crossings between phonons and magnons and the analysis of interlayer Ni-O chains associated with apical oxygen, magnon-phonon hybridization and charge-lattice coupling are proposed as two leading candidate mechanisms, while the specific mechanism remains an open question. These results establish a direct link between density-wave order and phonon transport in nickelates, highlight the active role of lattice degrees of freedom in their correlated normal state, and provide a sensitive probe of intertwined charge, spin, and lattice orders, with implications for understanding both their superconductivity and the multiple possible origins of phonon thermal Hall signals.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Colossal enhancement of thermoelectric performance via strain engineering in a two-dimensional Janus material
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Neelam Gupta, Shivani Rani, S. J. Ray
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: Strain engineering has emerged as a powerful technique for modulating diverse physical phenomena, including superconductivity, piezoelectricity, and magnetism. However, systematic tuning of thermoelectric and thermal transport properties remains relatively unexplored, particularly in two-dimensional systems. Janus transition-metal dichalcogenides, with their broken mirror symmetry, represent an emerging class of two-dimensional materials offering enhanced thermoelectric performance compared to their symmetric counterparts. In this work, we explore the thermoelectric properties of a VSeTe monolayer under biaxial compressive and tensile strain using first-principles calculations combined with Boltzmann transport theory. Analysis of the elastic constants and Poisson’s ratio confirms the feasibility of applying strain, while the phonon dispersion curves further demonstrate the dynamical stability of the proposed structure over the strain range from -1 % to + 2.5 % . Our findings reveal that strain engineering significantly modifies the electronic band structure and thermal transport properties, enabling remarkable enhancements in thermoelectric performance with a figure of merit (ZT) reaching 2.29 at room temperature under 2% tensile strain, representing a $$676% enhancement over the pristine value of 0.295. Overall, our mechanical, electronic, and thermoelectric analyses demonstrate that VSeTe monolayers exhibit exceptional strain tunability, establishing strain engineering as a highly effective route for achieving colossal enhancement in thermoelectric performance. These findings position VSeTe as a promising candidate for high-efficiency thermoelectric device application.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Pressure-enhanced thermoelectric transport in layered Bi2Se3 through band structure optimization
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Yuqi Gao, Dianzhen Wang, Shijie Hu, Dan Han, Jing Zou, Qiang Tao, Lu Wang, Yan Li, Pinwen Zhu
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: In general, the pressure-optimized thermoelectric transport of 2D layered materials is attributed to strengthened interlayer interactions that reduce the bandgap. However, this also introduces a pronounced bipolar effect and band edge sharpening, thereby limiting thermoelectric performance. In this study, taking layered Bi2Se3 as an example, we observed the onset temperature of the bipolar effect from approximately 387 K at 1 GPa to 459 K at 5 GPa. First-principles calculations show that pressure-induced interlayer compression modifies the coupling between band edge pz orbitals, leading to an increase in the bandgap from 0.21 eV at ambient pressure to 0.292 eV at 5 GPa. This suppresses the bipolar effect and is accompanied by conduction band flattening, which increases the density-of-states effective mass and enhances the Seebeck coefficient. Additionally, the native Se vacancies in Bi2Se3 introduce donor levels, and pressure-induced modulation of these donor levels promotes carrier thermally excited, leading to an increased carrier concentration. This not only suppresses the bipolar effect but also compensates for the reduction in carrier concentration caused by the pressure-widened bandgap, maintaining high electrical conductivity, consequently resulting in a record-high power factor of 2663 μW·m−1·K−2 at 5 GPa, 580 K, and an estimated maximum ZT value of 0.804 at 5 GPa, 580 K. This study provides insights into pressure-induced band structure optimization for enhanced thermoelectric performance under high pressure.

Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.title: Boosting thermoelectric performance of hydrothermal SnSe2 via Br doping-induced high carrier concentration and low thermal conductivity
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.authors: Chunlu Wu, Xinxin Wang, Zhuoming Xu, Ning Chen, Min Zhang, Zi-long Zhang, Yue-Xing Chen, Zhuang-Hao Zheng
Thermal Transport & Nonequilibrium Pheno.abstract: Anion-site doping represents a potent approach to tailor the electronic structure and transport properties of SnSe2. Herein, Br-doped SnSe2 bulk materials were successfully fabricated through a hydrothermal–annealing–sintering route, and the thermoelectric transport mechanisms were systematically investigated. Due to the valence electron discrepancy between Br and Se, the incorporation of Br into the matrix acts as a high-efficiency donor, triggering a degenerate semiconductor behavior. Consequently, the carrier concentration reached 2.38 × 1020 cm−3. Crucially, Br doping facilitates the microstructural texturing alignment during the consolidation process, thereby mitigating grain boundary potentials. This synergistic effect significantly boosts electrical conductivity, yielding a room-temperature power factor of 5.2 μW cm−1 K−2. Furthermore, the intensified point defect phonon scattering induced by Br substitution outweighs the weakened boundary scattering from grain growth, thereby suppressing the κ. As a result, a maximum ZT value of 0.47 is achieved in SnSe1.87Br0.13 at 773 K, which stands as a highly competitive performance among hydrothermally processed SnSe2. This work provides deep insights into the transport optimization of layered chalcogenides for green energy applications.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Reversible nonrelativistic magnon spin transport in ferroelastic altermagnets
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Haozhou Cai, Jian Wu, Weiyi Pan
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Magnons in antiferromagnetic (AFM) insulators facilitate low-dissipation, stray-field-free spin transport. However, achieving nonvolatile, field-free control over magnon spin currents remains elusive. Here, based on symmetry analysis, we propose a universal mechanism for the active manipulation of magnon spin transport via ferroelastic transitions in two-dimensional (2D) altermagnets (AMs)-a class of unconventional AFMs simultaneously exhibiting compensated magnetization and nonrelativistic spin splitting. We show that these transitions effectively reorient principal crystal axes and modulate the underlying magnetic exchange anisotropy. Consequently, this magnetoelastic coupling drives nonrelativistic anisotropic spin transport that is ferroelastically switchable without the need for external magnetic fields or Berry curvature, leading to sign reversals in the spin Seebeck and spin Nernst conductivities. We validate this mechanism using first-principles calculations and spin-model analyses of an AM CoTe2 monolayer. Our findings establish a symmetry-based magnetoelastic paradigm for the nonvolatile control of magnon spin transport in 2D AMs, opening new avenues toward energy-efficient, reconfigurable AFM magnonic devices.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Measurement of Magnonic Quantum Geometry
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: S. Kim, M. Stone, S. E. Nagler, A. D. Christianson, Jiabin Yu, S. Okamoto, H. Miao
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Quantum geometry plays a fundamental role in macroscopic quantum phenomena, including quantum Hall effects and flat-band superconductivity. However, since quantum geometry is encoded in wavefunctions rather than energy spectra, direct experimental characterization remains a formidable challenge. This challenge is particularly acute for quasiparticles in quantum materials, whose wavefunctions are generally inferred from effective low-energy models rather than measured directly. Here, we establish an experimental framework for characterizing the quantum geometry of magnons, a ubiquitous Bosonic quasiparticle of magnetically ordered states. We show that the inelastic neutron scattering (INS) cross-section measures geometric parameters of the spinor wavefunctions of ferromagnets. By tracking the energy- and momentum-dependent INS intensity, we extract the quantum geometric tensor without requiring detailed knowledge of microscopic spin-spin interactions. Our results establish magnons as an ideal arena for experimentally probing quantum geometry and open new avenues for exploring geometry-driven magnon transport and quantum Fisher information in magnetic materials.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Magnetic-field control of the Néel vector and magnon visibility in altermagnetic MnTe
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Tobias Weber, Niclas Heinsdorf, Shane Smolenski, Sawyer Beltz, Alexandre Ivanov, Andrea Piovano, Victor Mecoli, Sean Knapp, Ruiqi Tang, Amir Henderson, A. K. M. Ashiquzzaman Shawon, Taylor Pierce-James, Na Hyun Jo, Denis Karaiskaj
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Altermagnetic order gives rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting of electronic and magnonic excitations even in the absence of a net magnetization. Here, we investigate the magnetic field dependence of the spin-wave spectrum of altermagnetic α-MnTe using inelastic neutron scattering and linear spin-wave theory. An in-plane magnetic field continuously reorients the Néel vector by overcoming the weak crystalline anisotropy, while remaining small compared with the dominant exchange scale. We find that this reorientation leaves the magnon energies and line widths essentially unchanged, but strongly modifies the measured spectral intensity through the transverse-momentum projection. Our results demonstrate a clear separation between the soft orientational degree of freedom of the antiferromagnetic order and the robust exchange-dominated chiral magnon spectrum. This combination establishes α-MnTe as a platform for reconfigurable magnon coupling, in which external fields tune how excitations interact with polarized probes without substantially altering their frequency or coherence.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Directed Domain Wall Motion by Radio-Frequency Currents
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Lukas Fischer, Rouven Dreyer, Simon Arnold, Jae-Chun Jeon, Georg Woltersdorf, Stuart S. P. Parkin
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Magnetic domain walls (DWs) are central to emerging spintronic technologies for memory, logic and neuromorphic computing, where their controlled displacement is a key functionality. While current-induced DW motion driven by spin-orbit torques is well established under direct currents, it remains unclear how radio-frequency (RF) currents couple to DWs and whether they can generate directed motion under a symmetric periodic drive. Here we show that RF currents drive DW oscillations, which can be rectified into directed motion through symmetry breaking. Using time-resolved and static magneto-optical Kerr microscopy, we demonstrate that RF spin-orbit torques efficiently excite low-frequency DW oscillations well below the ferromagnetic resonance frequency. Whereas these oscillations remain symmetric in the absence of perturbations, symmetry breaking by a transverse magnetic field produces self-propulsion, while symmetry breaking by an initial current pulse gives rise to sustained DW motion. We further show that in initially uniform magnetic states, RF-driven expansion of a pulse-generated edge domain ultimately results in efficient RF-assisted magnetic switching. Together, these results establish a general framework for understanding how RF-driven DW oscillations are rectified into directed motion, providing new opportunities for their high-frequency control.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Ferromagnetic resonance signatures of edge states for distinguishing chiral and helical $p$-wave superconductors
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Shun Muto, Yuya Ominato, Takeo Kato, Mamoru Matsuo, Ai Yamakage
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: We theoretically investigate ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) modulation at interfaces between ferromagnetic insulators and two-dimensional chiral and helical $p$-wave superconductors. We evaluate the surface dynamical spin susceptibility, including both edge and bulk quasiparticle excitations. For momentum-conserving interfacial exchange at zero temperature, the edge contribution to the Gilbert damping exhibits distinct frequency scalings for the excitation energies well above the spectral broadening, $\hbarω\gg2δ$: $δ/(\hbarω)^{2}$ for the chiral state and $1/\hbarω$ for the helical state. For a clean superconducting boundary, edge-induced Ising spin anisotropy persists even when interfacial exchange disorder randomizes momentum transfer. The low-energy edge response is suppressed when the magnetization aligns with the edge-state spin axis. These results establish FMR modulation as a probe complementary to existing methods for distinguishing the chiral and helical states and constraining their $d$-vector directions.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Direction-dependent coherent-dissipative indirect coupling in cavity magnonics
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Zhenhui Hao, Kang An, Xu Zhang, Chi Zhang, Guozhi Chai
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: We demonstrate direction-dependent coherent-dissipative indirect coupling in cavity magnonics. A photon-like self-cavity resonance of a yttrium iron garnet disk first hybridizes with the ferromagnetic resonance to form magnon–photon polaritons. The lower polariton subsequently interacts with the effective cavity response near an interference induced antiresonance formed by adjacent resonances of a two port quadrant-stadium cavity. Under otherwise identical experimental conditions, the same hybridization exhibits level repulsion in forward transmission S21 and level-attraction-like behavior in backward transmission S12, corresponding to coherent-dominated and dissipative-dominated responses, respectively. Independent phase measurements yield distinct directional phase responses, which are directly used as the phase parameters in a hierarchical input-output model. The model captures the principal direction-dependent hybridization features and relates the reversal of the coupling character to the effective phase structure of the polariton cavity port scattering pathway. The resulting nonreciprocity produces compound isolation in opposite directions within two distinct and nonoverlapping frequency windows, providing a route toward multiband nonreciprocal signal processing.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Controlling valley polarization and transport properties of monolayer and bilayer Co 2 CF 2 by applied electric field: Symmetry analysis and first principles calculations
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Jingjing Wan, Kang Jia, Xiaohong Zheng, Xuan Gao, Peng Jiang, Chuanjia Tong, Junqin Shi, Xiaoli Fan, Tengfei Cao
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Two-dimensional multiferroic Co2CF2 seamlessly integrates ferroelectricity, ferromagnetism, and valley polarization within an atomic layer limit, serving as an ideal platform for low-power, nonvolatile spintronic devices. Achieving effective electrical control over band topology and quantum transport is central to advancing 2D multiferroic applications, yet a unified symmetry-guided understanding remains lacking. In this work, by combining symmetry analysis and first-principles quantum transport calculations, we systematically investigate the electric-polarization control of electronic, topological, and tunneling transport properties in both monolayer and bilayer Co2CF2. For monolayer Co2CF2, we establish fundamental symmetry mapping rules (P, PT, Mz, MzT), showing how polarization reversal between symmetry-related endpoint configurations can reverse valley polarization or anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC), depending on the operation, while preserving the type of magnetic order. Extending this symmetry framework to monolayer-based lateral magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs), we uncover symmetry-dependent transmission contrasts that yield an ultrahigh tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) ratio up to 3.65×105%. To introduce additional degrees of freedom, we further construct bilayer Co2CF2 configurations, where interlayer sliding ferroelectricity and interlayer antiferromagnetic coupling synergistically modulate energy band topology and tunneling transmission, suggesting a route to multi-state nonvolatile TMR control through polarization and interlayer sliding. This work provides a unified, symmetry-guided design strategy for 2D multiferroics and lays a solid theoretical foundation for next-generation, high-performance spintronic devices.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Spin Berry curvature and intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in noncentrosymmetric A B X compounds
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Arijeet Sarangi, Rajib Sarkar, Sudip Chakraborty
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: The spin Hall effect (SHE) lies at the heart of spin orbit based spintronics, providing a mechanism through which charge currents generate transverse spin currents. In this work, we use density functional theory to study the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity (SHC) in a family of non-centrosymmetric ABX compounds crystallizing in the hexagonal P 6 3 m c structure. Broken inversion symmetry, along with spin orbit coupling (SOC), can give rise to nontrivial spin Berry curvature textures in these materials. We compute SHC for a representative set of compounds and observe a wide variation in its magnitude across different chemical compositions. This allows us to segregate the materials into distinct regimes characterized by relatively high, intermediate and low SHC values. The energy-dependent SHC further indicates that hole doping or electrostatic gating can tune the response toward its maxima below the Fermi level. To gain insight into these variations, we evaluate corresponding electronic structures and spin Berry curvature distributions, identifying notable differences in their behavior around the Fermi level. These variations may be attributed to the SOC induced band features including interband hybridization, and the position of spin Berry curvature hotspots relative to the Fermi energy. Furthermore, substitution on the A, B, and X sublattices substantially modifies the electronic structure and can also lower the crystal symmetry, thereby reshaping SOC driven band splittings and the resulting SHC, which highlights pronounced compositional tunability. In several compounds, inversion symmetry breaking induces Rashba type spin splitting, and a subset exhibits signatures of nontrivial band topology, including surface state features. Our results offer a broad, chemically resolved picture of intrinsic spin Hall responses in this structural family, and underscore the role that symmetry and SOC might play in sculpting spin Berry curvature landscapes and spin transport behavior in non-centrosymmetric systems.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Predicting the generation of tunable nonreciprocal spin waves mediated by interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in magnonic heterostructures
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Cameron A. McEleney, Karen L. Livesey, Robert E. Camley, Rair Macêdo
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Thin, metallic magnetic films can support nonreciprocal spin waves due to the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI). However, these films typically have high damping, making spin wave propagation distances short (less than one micrometer). In this work, we theoretically study a thin ferromagnetic strip with iDMI and excite spin waves by driving a central segment of the strip. Spin waves propagate with different amplitudes to the left versus to the right from the driving region (i.e. nonreciprocity occurs) due to the iDMI. Our calculation based on spin-wave-dispersion plus our micromagnetic simulations both show that changing the driving segment width, driving frequency and static applied field strength tunes the nonreciprocity. Our calculation based on spin-wave-dispersion, using a so-called "overlap function" will allow researchers to predict conditions of maximum nonreciprocity, without the need for computational solvers. Moreover, to circumvent the issue of short propagation distances, we propose a geometry where iDMI is only present in the driving region and low-damping materials comprise the remainder of the strip. Our calculations show significant spin wave amplitudes over several microns from the excitation region.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Computational Modeling of Sublattice Magnetization in CoTb/Co/CoTb Magnetic Multilayer Nanojunctions Between Cobalt Leads
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Sushita Sharma, Vinod Ashokan
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: In this work, we study the sublattice nano-magnetic behavior of CoTb/Co/CoTb sandwiched between semi-infinite cobalt leads. To perform the analysis, we use the Ising spin-based effective field theory (EFT), which enables us to determine the relevant magnetic exchange parameters for elemental cobalt JCo-Co and terbium JTb-Tb. The exchange interaction parameters are determined by fitting the magnetization calculated using the Ising effective-field theory to the experimentally measured temperature-dependent magnetization curves. This fitting procedure yields the exchange constants for Co and Tb, along with their respective Curie temperatures. We use the magnetic exchange parameter obtained using Ising EFT-based method is then seeded on to mean field theory (MFT) to calculate the sublattice magnetizations of CoTb/Co/CoTb arranged between semi-infinite cobalt leads. The sublattice magnetizations for every atomic layer and corresponding lattice sites in the layered ferrimagnetic nanostructures are computed separately. This allows us to analyze spin-site-specific parameters, magnetic moments, magnetization, and ferrimagnetic compensation behavior for varying eutectic compositions, particularly for \(c \leq 0.5\). The results give enhanced insight into magnetic phenomena at the local level and their general relevance in the ultra-thin layered ferrimagnetic structure dynamics confined between semi-infinite cobalt electrodes. These results are needed for the understanding of magnon transport phenomena and consequent magnetic amplification effects and are crucial to the development of spintronic technologies. Most importantly, to date, no first-principles or density functional theory research exists for sublattice magnetization in such multilayered systems. The versatile approach established in this work can also be applied to other nanostructured magnetic systems

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Parametric frequency mixing in synthetic antiferromagnets driven by surface acoustic waves
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Long Cheng, Bing Lv, Yuantian Pan, Xu Liu, Yongzuo Wang, Zhongjie Yan, Cunxu Gao
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Parametric frequency mixing (PFM) is a fundamental nonlinear process in magnetization dynamics, essential for generating new frequencies for spintronic and magnonic applications. Previous studies of magnetoelastic PFM in single ferromagnetic layers established harmonic generation, and a subsequent experiment identified DC offsets. However, an explicit analytical expression for the DC response comparable to those for the fundamental and second-harmonic amplitudes is not available. In this work, we develop a controlled second-order description for a canted synthetic antiferromagnet (SAF) that treats the signed DC and complex second-harmonic responses on the same footing. The analysis separates the magnetoelastic and interlayer exchange coupling (IEC) source phasors without changing the equilibrium or linear susceptibility, while retaining finite-wave-vector propagation and layer parity. Analytical calculations and fully coupled numerical simulations show that both responses scale quadratically with the acoustic strain. The two source channels interfere constructively or destructively in the individual layers, and a predominantly acoustic fundamental generates an IEC source with predominantly optical parity, yielding a total second-order response with finite optical content. These results provide an explicit DC treatment and identify a layer-symmetry-distinct IEC-mediated second-order mixing channel in canted SAFs.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Correlated route to antiferromagnetic spintronics
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Joel Bobadilla, Alberto Camjayi
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Antiferromagnets are attractive for spintronics owing to their vanishing net magnetization and ultrafast spin dynamics, yet their spin-compensated electronic structure has long confined them to passive roles. Here we identify a symmetry selection rule that overcomes this limitation: in a collinear antiferromagnet, a spin-polarized dc charge current requires the simultaneous breaking of particle–hole symmetry and of the equivalence between the two magnetic sublattices, either one alone leaving the polarization identically zero. We demonstrate the rule in the doped antiferromagnetic Hubbard model within dynamical mean-field theory: doping and a uniform magnetic field each break one of the two symmetries, and electronic correlations convert the resulting asymmetries into a sizable, field-tunable polarization of the charge current. The polarization is largest deep in the ordered phase and reverses sign at an emergent compensation point, set by the hierarchy of spin- dependent scattering rates and not dictated by symmetry, at which the dominant conducting spin species is interchanged. In correlated altermagnetic Hubbard models, the same two symmetries are broken structurally, by the sublattice-alternating hopping pattern: the field-driven mechanism identified here and the altermagnetic one are two realizations of a single selection rule. Electronic correlations thus emerge as an active ingredient for spintronics in structurally conventional collinear antiferromagnets.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Interfacial Effects of Thermal Reorganization on Charge and Spin Transport in Organic Spin Valves
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Zihao Liu, Yunzhe Ke, Hajar Komekoz, Shuai Gu, Rico Ehrler, Chen Wang, Olav Hellwig, Frank Ortmann, Dietrich R. T. Zahn, Carsten Deibel, Michael Sommer, Shuaishuai Ding, Georgeta Salvan
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Organic semiconductors are attractive for spintronic applications owing to their weak spin-orbit coupling, small hyperfine interactions, mechanical flexibility, and tunable electronic properties. Organic spin valves (OSVs) provide a representative platform for investigating spin-dependent transport. However, the magnetoresistance (MR) response is highly sensitive to the ferromagnetic electrode/organic semiconductor interface (spinterface). Variations in interfacial morphology, chemical interaction, energy-level alignment, and spin polarization can strongly affect spin injection, transport, and detection, making reproducible OSV performance difficult to achieve. Here, we investigate how in situ thermal annealing affects the electrical and magnetotransport properties of complete NDI-based OSVs. Two top-electrode configurations are compared: directly evaporated Co/Au and transferred Gr (graphene)/Co/Au. Both as-cast devices exhibit clear MR responses, with a stronger absolute response observed for the transferred-electrode device. After in situ annealing, the resistance of both device types increases substantially, and no reproducible MR response is resolved, despite the enhanced structural order observed in companion films and an approximately 36-fold increase in the effective vertical conductivity extracted from electron-only devices. This contrasting behavior indicates that improved bulk order alone is insufficient to ensure enhanced spin-valve performance. Instead, annealing-induced changes in interfacial contact, contact homogeneity, and local current distribution can become dominant in determining the complete-device response. These results emphasize the critical role of spinterface stability and interface engineering in achieving reliable and thermally robust OSV operation.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Magnons in α -Fe2O3 microdisks: From thermal to coherent excitation
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Jinlong Wang, Katharina Müller, Haishen Peng, Janine Gückelhorn, Wenjie Song, Lutong Sheng, Jilei Chen, Song Liu, Dapeng Yu, Stephan Geprägs, Matthias Althammer, Haiming Yu
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Hematite is a prototypical antiferromagnetic insulator for spintronic and magnonic applications, yet controlled studies of coherent magnons in thin films remain challenging due to strain sensitivity and spatial inhomogeneity. Here, we investigate magnon excitations in lithographically patterned hematite microdisks and obtain reproducible magnon spectra from multiple individual microdisks. Brillouin light scattering reveals bulk-like field-dependent thermal magnon resonances with an ultralow effective damping parameter on the order of ∼10−5. Coherent magnons are further excited using a strip line antenna adjacent to the microdisk, revealing a power-dependent frequency blue shift accompanied by a nonlinear evolution of the coherent response under strong microwave driving. Field-dependent analysis indicates a power-dependent increase in the effective magnetic anisotropy field, suggesting a tunable nonlinear response of antiferromagnetic magnons in laterally confined microdisks. These results establish patterned hematite thin films as a platform for exploring coherent and nonlinear antiferromagnetic magnon dynamics.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Chirality-Odd Readout of Coherence-Mediated Magnon Spin Transport
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Yanmeng Lei, Ji Zou, Sanchar Sharma, Tao Yu
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Structural chirality is ubiquitous in magnets, yet its impact on spin transport in insulators remains largely unexplored, with only a few recent experiments offering the first glimpses. Here we predict the chiral response in the electric spin injection-detection configuration in both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic spirals. The screw symmetry of the spiral forbids any nonzero diagonal element of the magnon spin matrix: every eigenmode is linearly polarized and carries no spin, so spin transport is mediated entirely by superposition between distinct modes. Reversing chirality flips the magnon spin along the spiral axis and the injected quantum coherence in lockstep, leaving the associated injected spin current invariant. Spiral chirality acts instead at the detection interface, where electron--magnon scattering amplitude is reversed and causes the magnon accumulation to be read out as a voltage of opposite sign. This interfacial readout is consistent with reversed first-harmonic voltage under electric-field switching in multiferroic BiFeO$_3$, establishing structural chirality as an intrinsic control parameter for magnon coherence and its electrical readout.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Optically modulated field-dependent electrical response in a non-collinear antiferromagnet/ferromagnet heterostructure
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Adrielson Dias, André José, José Lucas, Rodrigo Cristian, José Holanda
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: The interplay among optical, electrical, and magnetic stimuli offers opportunities to control the functional response of spintronic heterostructures. Here, we investigate the field-dependent electrical response of MgO/IrMn$_3$/Py/Au under radio-frequency (RF) excitation, white-light illumination, and direct-current (DC) bias. Under a 20 MHz RF signal with a nominal power of 2 W, the measured voltage in the dark remains at several tens of nanovolts. Upon illumination with approximately 1 W of white light, a pronounced field-dependent feature emerges around 315--320 Oe, reaching 0.9--1.0 $μ$V. The illumination-associated differential voltage is approximately 0.95 $μ$V. A DC current of 1 mA produces a response of approximately 1 $μ$V, while the simultaneous application of RF, DC, and optical excitation increases the voltage to approximately 1.8 $μ$V. Magnetic characterization reveals exchange bias with a blocking temperature near 380 K, while electrical resistance measurements show a pronounced dependence on magnetic-field orientation, consistent with the anisotropic response of the heterostructure. These results demonstrate that the field-dependent electrical response can be modulated through combined optical and electrical excitation, involving magneto-optical interactions and spin-dependent transport phenomena, potentially including spin Hall-related contributions and the magnetic spin Hall effect. This work provides insights into coupled optical, electrical, and magnetic-field effects in heterostructures based on non-collinear antiferromagnets and ferromagnetic layers.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Temperature-Driven Evolution of Magnetization Dynamics in Cobalt-Doped Fe$_5$GeTe$_2$
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Sourabh Singh, Soumik Aon, Andrew F. May, Joost Ridderbos, Ramanathan Mahendiran, Wilfred G. van der Wiel
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Understanding magnetization dynamics in metallic van der Waals ferromagnets is essential to uncover their magnetic interactions and evaluate their potential for high-frequency spintronics applications. In this study, we investigate the temperature-dependent magnetization dynamics of a single crystal of cobalt-doped $Fe_{5}GeTe_{2}$ (CFGT) using broadband ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) spectroscopy. At high temperatures, the FMR response is dominated by a single broad resonance that shifts toward lower magnetic fields upon cooling. Fits to the frequency dependence of the resonance field and linewidth yield an effective $g$ factor of approximately 2.45 and an effective Gilbert damping parameter of approximately 0.15 near room temperature. The effective magnetic anisotropy evolves strongly with temperature, with an increasingly pronounced easy-plane contribution upon cooling toward 200 K. Below approximately 200 K, an additional resonance emerges and evolves into a distinct two-mode response that persists to the lowest measured temperature of 25 K. The two branches exhibit different temperature dependences of their resonance fields and linewidths, and the emergence of the additional mode is not accompanied by a comparably pronounced anomaly in the static magnetization. These results reveal a dynamical crossover in CFGT that is not readily apparent from bulk magnetometry and highlight the sensitivity of FMR to the magnetic behavior of chemically substituted van der Waals ferromagnets.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Enhanced spintronic terahertz emission from Fe/Pt heterostructures enabled by naturally oxidized Cu capping layers
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Chao Zhou, Lei Hao, Yaxuan Jin, Shaohua Zhang, Xianguo Jiang, Ning Yang, Tong Fu, Yuxi Guo, Chao Lu, Wendeng Huang, Jia Xu
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on Fe/Pt heterostructures rely on inverse spin Hall conversion of laser-induced ultrafast spin currents. Here, we show that naturally oxidized Cu capping enhances THz emission from Fe/Pt. After natural oxidation, the THz amplitude of Fe/Pt/CuOx reaches up to approximately 1.4 times that of the Fe/Pt reference. Control experiments show that the THz response of Fe/CuOx is too weak to account for the enhancement observed in the trilayer, whereas inserting Cu between Fe and Pt strongly suppresses the emission. Angle-resolved x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a partially oxidized, nonuniform CuOx layer with a pronounced depth-dependent oxidation gradient, while Al2O3 capping strongly suppresses the oxidation-dependent THz evolution. Pt- and Cu-thickness-dependent measurements further reveal an optimized thickness window and highlight the interface-sensitive nature of the enhancement. These results are consistent with an additional inverse orbital Rashba–Edelstein-related contribution at the chemically asymmetric Pt/CuOx interface, which assists the dominant Pt-based inverse spin Hall conversion. Our findings establish naturally oxidized Cu capping as a simple route for enhancing and tuning Fe/Pt spintronic THz emitters through oxide-assisted interface engineering.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Electrically switchable spintronics in a multiferroic altermagnet
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Martin Latorre, Sebastian Allende, Alvaro S. Nunez
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: We introduce a minimal model of a two-dimensional lattice that, upon spontaneous symmetry breaking, simultaneously develops altermagnetic order, a finite electric polarization, and a spin-polarized transport response, all of which are controlled by an external electric field. By coupling a dimerized altermagnet to an external electric field, we show that the three order parameters are not merely compatible but dynamically entangled, so that switching one (for instance, reversing the polarization with an electric field) necessarily reconfigures the other two. We show that this model offers a clear physical blueprint for designing next-generation spintronic logic and pure spin current memdevices that merge the ultrafast, stray-field-free advantages of compensated magnets with the low-power switching architectures of ferroelectrics.

Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.title: Altermagnetism in Mn2SeX (X = O, S, Te) for magnetic tunnel junctions
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.authors: Han Li, Xiao Liu, Keqian He, Xiaoran Du, Chuan Xie, Sicong Zhu
Spintronics & Spin Seebeck Effect.abstract: Altermagnets uniquely combine compensated magnetic moments with broken PT symmetry, offering ferromagnet-like spin polarization alongside antiferromagnetic stability and ultrafast dynamics. Leveraging these assets, AM-based devices hold immense promise for magnetic tunnel junctions, Hall sensors, and magnetocaloric applications. Guided by spin space group theory, we break the PT symmetry of MnSe via atomic substitution, yielding d-wave altermagnetic Mn2SeX (X = O, S, Te) with favorable spin electronic properties. Our analysis reveals that the rotational symmetry introduced by partial Se substitution serves as the microscopic origin of the non-relativistic spin splitting. Leveraging these superior spin transport characteristics, we demonstrate a tunneling magnetoresistance ratio of 376.3% in Mn2SeTe-based AMTJs. Our work not only establishes a theoretical paradigm for designing novel altermagnets but also computationally demonstrates their substantial potential for high-performance MTJ applications.

Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.title: Strain-induced spin reorientation transition and associated anomalies of magnetization dynamics in epitaxial Y 3 Fe 5 O 12 films
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.abstract: Ferrimagnetic insulator yttrium iron garnet (YIG) is distinguished by very low magnetic damping, which makes it favorable for experimental investigations of spin dynamics and suitable for various device applications. This paper presents a theoretical study of the effects of substrate-induced strains on the equilibrium magnetization direction, ferromagnetic resonance, and spin-wave dispersion in single-crystalline YIG films. The magnetic free energy is calculated with the account of the magnetoelastic coupling between spins and lattice strains and mechanical boundary conditions imposed on a single-domain film epitaxially grown on a thick dissimilar substrate. The energy minimization reveals the existence of a spin reorientation transition (SRT) in strained YIG films with both (111) and (001) crystallographic orientations. When the film is subjected to an isotropic biaxial in-plane strain , an abrupt SRT takes place in the (111)-oriented film at a critical tensile strain SRT in the absence of magnetic field. In contrast, the magnetization in the (001)-oriented film gradually rotates between the 110 and 001 directions in a narrow range of the tensile strain . Remarkably, the calculation of the resonance frequency res of the strained YIG film shows that res strongly decreases near the threshold strain, at which the magnetization becomes orthogonal to the film plane. Strain-induced changes in the dispersion relation of forward volume spin waves propagating in the perpendicularly magnetized YIG films are predicted as well. A strain-mediated electrical control of the spin-wave dispersion via mechanical coupling to a piezoelectric substrate is proposed for YIG films.

Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.title: Metamagnetism driven magnetocaloric crossover with exchange bias in Eu 2 CoRuO 6
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.authors: Amitava Ghosh, Dipak Mazumdar, Rajashri R. Urkude, Shubham Patil, Aswin Kumar Burma, Biplab Ghosh, Koushik Pal, Chanchal Sow
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.abstract: The mutual dependence of lattice symmetries and magnetic exchange interactions helps in tuning the magnetic ground state in double perovskites. Here we report the nature of 3d-4d interaction and role of anti-site disorder in governing the magnetic, magnetocaloric and exchange bias properties in a novel double perovskite Eu2CoRuO6. Two Eu2CoRuO6 samples were synthesized with different cooling protocols in order to control anti-site disorder. The x-ray diffraction and extended x-ray absorption fine structure analysis confirm nearly 17% and 33% anti-site disorder in the two samples. Theoretical electronic structure calculation reveals the Co-O-Ru interaction to be ferromagnetic in a perfectly ordered Eu2CoRuO6. However, lack of saturation in the magnetization measurements is attributed to the presence of anti-site disorder. The high-field magnetization decreases by 42% due to a 16% increase in anti-site disorder. The temperature dependent magnetization studies uncover Ru-O-Co ferromagnetic transition around 54 K and low temperature antiferromagnetic transition corresponding to Ru-O-Ru and Co-O-Co interactions. Interestingly, an inverse to conventional magnetocaloric crossover along with exchange bias is noticed below 40 K in the sample with 17% disorder. The simultaneous occurrence of magnetocaloric crossover and exchange bias phenomena is linked with anti-site disorder and metamagnetism.

Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.title: Hidden interfacial magnetism in RuO$_2$ heterostructures revealed by a superconducting spin switch
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.authors: Tetsuma Mandokoro, Hisakazu Matsuki, Shutaro Karube, Rodrigo de las Heras, Andrei Mazanik, Akihiro Yamada, Fugo Tokoro, Susumu Hirata, Ryusuke Hisatomi, Yoichi Shiota, Vitaly N. Golovach, F. Sebastian Bergeret, Teruo Ono
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.abstract: RuO$_2$, once the flagship altermagnetic candidate, is now believed to be nonmagnetic in the bulk, yet weak, static and spatially inhomogeneous magnetism emerges at its surfaces and interfaces. Where this magnetism resides, what stabilises it, and whether it is connected to these states remain open questions. Here we address these questions at the Nb/RuO$_2$ interface using a superconducting spin switch. A GdN/Nb/RuO$_2$ trilayer allows interfacial exchange-field alignment to tune the superconducting transition temperature of Nb, probing interfacial magnetism inaccessible to conventional magnetometry. The switch reveals a hidden magnetic subsystem, which we attribute to a thin RuO$_x$ redox layer formed as Nb scavenges oxygen from RuO$_2$. This layer behaves as a weak and magnetically hard ferromagnet with vacancy-induced anisotropy. Furthermore, supercurrent amplifies the switching efficiency, making the probe sensitivity tunable in situ. Superconducting spin switches thus emerge as a quantitative low-temperature probe of hidden magnetism at buried interfaces.

Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.title: Magnetic proximity beyond the interface: Layer-sequence-dependent exchange in WSe 2 / CrI 3 heterostructures
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.authors: Natalie Kuhn, Marc Schütte, Joachim Emming, Felix Hellenkamp, Leo Dreyer, Frank Volmer, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Lutz Waldecker, Christoph Stampfer, Bernd Beschoten
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.abstract: Magnetic proximity effects in transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD)/2D-magnet heterostructures are often described in terms of the magnetization of the interfacial magnetic layer. Here, we show that this picture is sufficient to describe the neutral-exciton valley splitting of the TMD, but incomplete for its hole-doped electronic structure. We study a gate-tunable van der Waals heterostructure composed of monolayer WSe 2 in direct contact with trilayer CrI 3 . By combining spatially and helicity-resolved reflection-contrast spectroscopy with magnetic circular dichroism, we identify two distinct magnetic domains in the trilayer CrI 3 : one with purely antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling and one with a mixed antiferromagnetic (AFM)/ferromagnetic (FM) coupling. In both domains, the sign of the neutral-exciton valley splitting of WSe 2 switches with the magnetization reversal of the adjacent CrI 3 layer. In contrast, helicity-resolved positive-trion spectroscopy of WSe 2 reveals a qualitatively different response. While the AFM domain shows a strongly helicity-selective trion resonance, the mixed AFM/FM domain exhibits trion resonances in both helicities. This behavior disappears when all CrI 3 layers are aligned in a parallel magnetization direction. Our results demonstrate that the positive-trion response is sensitive to the magnetic configuration of CrI 3 beyond the directly adjacent layer, revealing a magnetic proximity response that cannot be described solely by the interfacial magnetization.

Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.title: Reflective Spin Wave Filtering Limiters with Bandpass to Bandstop Bifurcation
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.abstract: Spin wave (SW) filters using thin-film yttrium iron garnet are an attractive technology for reconfigurable and software defined radio (SDR) systems in which parameters such as channel frequency or transmit power are adjusted in real time to efficiently utilize constrained spectrum resources. Operating in congested electromagnetic environments leave communication systems vulnerable to damage or disruption from strong interference and jamming. Therefore, frequency tunable filters and power limiters are needed to support SDR operation on the physical layer. Here, we report a frequency tunable bandpass filtering limiter which reflects excess above threshold power using a network of nonlinear SW resonators in a ladder filter topology. The reported devices show insertion losses as low as 3.29 dB, isolation above 14.22 dB, center frequency tuning over more than two octaves from 4.75 GHz to 21.08 GHz, fast transient response of 14.01 ns, and low transient spike leakage. A physics-informed nonlinear SW model is discussed and a method to simulate and design networks of nonlinear resonators is introduced.

Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.title: Chiral quantum batteries
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.authors: Rong-Fang Liu, Wan-Lu Song, Wan-Li Yang, Hua Guan, Jun-Hong An
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.abstract: Quantum batteries (QBs) offer compelling advantages over conventional ones in terms of superior energy density, ultrafast charging, and high conversion efficiency. However, their realization is hampered by decoherence, which causes incomplete charging, rapid self-discharging, and reduced extractable work. Here, we propose a quantum-compatible battery architecture based on a chiral magnonic platform. It comprises two yttrium iron garnet (YIG) spheres, one serving as the charger and the other as the QB, coupled to a waveguide. The unique chiral coupling between magnons and the guided electromagnetic fields breaks inversion symmetry, inducing both nonreciprocal energy flow and coherent interference between the charger and QB. Their synergy endows our QB with a 34-fold increase in energy capacity and a 55-fold boost in extractable work compared to its achiral counterpart in an experimentally accessible regime. Our scheme harnesses the decoherence induced by the common electromagnetic fields, which enables the robustness and wireless-like remote charging features of the QB. Without relying on quantum resource and being representable by classical dynamics, our architecture provides a viable route toward robust and remote-charging of QBs.

Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.title: Single Spin Hall Conversion in the Hall Response of Magnetic-Insulator/Heavy-Metal Bilayers Identified by Odd Spin-Hall-Angle Dependence
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.authors: Akashdeep Akashdeep, Ewiese Mohammad Ababneh, Botros Gerges Mikhail Fenhas, Duc Minh Tran, Mathias Kläui, Steven S. -L. Zhang, Vivek Amin, Gerhard Jakob, Timo Kuschel
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.abstract: The Hall response of magnetic-insulator/heavy-metal bilayers is usually ascribed to two successive spin Hall conversions and is therefore expected to be even in the spin Hall angle. Using distinct magnetic-field windows, we separate the Hall voltage of yttrium iron garnet bilayers with Ta and Pt of opposite spin Hall angle into contributions from magnetization- and magnetic-field-driven precession as well as from ordinary Hall effect. The field-driven component reverses sign between Ta and Pt, revealing a Hall response odd-in-spin-Hall-angle. The magnetization-driven component also has opposite signs for Ta and Pt, except for the thinnest heavy-metal layers. A drift-diffusion model with interface-generated spin currents describes this behavior: the field-driven component is predominantly carried by a single spin Hall conversion, and the magnetization-driven component is consistent with one as well. Other potential explanations, based on a description with a finite imaginary spin-mixing conductance rather than interface-generated spin currents, require unusually large values of this conductance, making this mechanism unlikely. Our findings advance the understanding of Hall responses in magnetic-insulator/heavy-metal bilayers toward a more general description.

Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.title: Superconductivity in Fe-rich FeTe nanosheets grown by chemical vapor deposition
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.authors: Shaojie Liu, Shuxi Wang, Xuewei Wang, Yuanbin Qin, Xueyan Dong, Xiaoyu Wang, Lin Zou, Lei Zhang, Jie Pan, Qihong Chen, Zhe Wang
Magnetic Interfaces & YIG/Pt.abstract: Tetragonal FeTe is structurally simple but highly stoichiometry-sensitive platform in which excess iron usually stabilizes antiferromagnetism and suppresses superconductivity. Although chemical vapor deposition (CVD) provides a scalable route to two-dimensional FeTe crystals, superconductivity in CVD-grown FeTe remains rare. Here, we report superconducting Fe-rich tetragonal Fe1.22Te nanosheets grown by CVD on atomically flat mica. The devices exhibit a superconducting onset near 11.9 K, accompanied by a sharp resistance drop with a finite residual resistance tail, nonlinear I-V with a characteristic critical current, and a large extrapolated upper critical field far exceeding the Pauli paramagnetic limit. Antiferromagnetic order persists into the superconducting regime, as evidenced by the exchange bias effect in Fe3GeTe2/Fe1.22Te heterostructures. Atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy directly reveals nanoscale variations in the interstitial-Fe distribution, with interstitial-Fe-rich regions adjacent to regions showing no detectable interstitial-Fe contrast. These observations together support a percolative phase-separated picture, in which FeTe-like superconducting regions are embedded in an antiferromagnetic Fe-rich matrix. Our work demonstrates CVD growth on mica as an effective route to superconducting Fe1+yTe nanosheets and provides insight into superconductivity in FeTe with nanoscale interstitial-Fe inhomogeneity.

Polarized Neutron Reflectometry.title: Effects of probe size, shape, and probe-surface interactions in imaging multilayer island growth, coalescence, and formation of a smooth film
Polarized Neutron Reflectometry.authors: Ismael S. S. Carrasco, Tiago J. Oliveira, Fábio D. A. Aarão Reis
Polarized Neutron Reflectometry.abstract: Recent studies of deposition onto weakly interacting substrates have revealed multilayer island growth, followed by smooth-film formation upon island coalescence. However, for C60 films, the roughness peak measured by atomic force microscopy (AFM) was significantly lower than that obtained by X-ray reflectometry (XRR), suggesting tip-sample convolution effects. We investigate this problem using kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations of such films and models of probe-surface interactions for AFM imaging modes. To model the non-contact mode, surface profiles are transformed by averaging heights over regions matching the probe-tip width. A roughness peak remains if the probe width L is smaller than the average island distance, but its height decreases with L and its position is slightly displaced. In the contact-mode model with cylindrical probes and hard-core interactions, the peak also decreases and shifts significantly to smaller thicknesses, indicating apparently faster island coalescence. Thus, SPM images under these conditions may underestimate film-thickness nonuniformity in deposits with coalescing islands. Instead, models of sharp pyramidal or conical probes with hard-core interactions produce deviations in the roughness peaks only for large L, although such sharp tips are difficult to realize experimentally. A geometric model of cuboid island growth and coalescence quantitatively confirms the effects of contact modes and probe shapes observed in the simulations. The results suggest that post-growth processes, such as island coarsening and dewetting, may have occurred in the recently studied C60 film between the XRR and AFM measurements.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Vestiges of magnon fractionalization in the quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet rouaite Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ with alternating ferro- and antiferromagnetic $S=\frac{1}{2}$ chains
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Darren C. Peets, Satoshi Nishimoto, Denys Y. Kononenko, Oleg Janson, Aswathi Mannathanath Chakkingal, Anton A. Kulbakov, Kaushick K. Parui, Harald O. Jeschke, Ellen Häußler, James P. Tellam, J. Ross Stewart, Dmytro S. Inosov
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Ferro- and antiferromagnetic quantum spin chains host qualitatively distinct elementary excitations --- magnons ($S=1$, bosonic quasiparticles) and spinons ($S=\frac{1}{2}$, fractionalized quasiparticles), respectively. Weakly coupled networks of both chain types therefore provide an ideal platform for exploring spinon-magnon coupling and the hybridization of sharp magnon modes with spinon continua. Here we investigate the spin-excitation spectrum of the frustrated quantum magnet rouaite, Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ --- a model realization of weakly coupled ferro- and antiferromagnetic Cu$^{2+}$ spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ chains. The frustrated interchain interactions, while weaker than the dominant intrachain exchange, are sufficient to stabilize a long-range-ordered state that is not reproduced by classical calculations. Neutron spectroscopy reveals a spectrum of well-defined spin waves associated with both types of chains, with clear signatures of hybridization but no observable spinon continuum. Certain magnon branches resulting from this hybridization exhibit substantial broadening near the zone center. We attribute this to vestiges of spinon fractionalization persisting partway through the dimensional crossover from isolated quantum spin chains to a 2D network of frustrated spins.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Discovery of Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line Topological State in strongly correlated material CeAuAl$_3$
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Hari Bhandari, Kevin Allen, Kuan-Sen Lin, Yuan Fang, Arushi, Karthik Rao, Mounica Mahankali, Sanu Mishra, Jian-Xin Zhu, Christopher Lane, Qimiao Si, Emilia Morosan
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Kramers nodal lines (KNLs) are predicted in all achiral, non-centrosymmetric crystal structures, and yet there are very few experimental realizations of KNLs, only in weakly correlated systems. Especially, their realization in strongly correlated systems remains unexplored. Here we investigate KNL topology in the non-centrosymmetric, achiral Kondo lattice CeAuAl$_3$, using magnetotransport, thermodynamic measurements, density functional theory (DFT), and tight-binding toy model calculations. We find that CeAuAl$_3$ hosts KNLs in the $\mathitΓ\text{-}Z$ and $X\text{-}P$ directions, protected by time-reversal and mirror symmetries. Breaking of these crystalline symmetries, along with time-reversal symmetry via spin polarization, lifts the KNL degeneracy, which, in turn, generates Berry curvature resulting in an intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE). More importantly, CeAuAl$_3$ shows large AHE not only below the magnetic ordering temperature $T_N$ but rather below the Kondo temperature. This underscores the role of the Kondo correlations in bringing the KNLs at the Fermi surface rather than at accidental energies, as would be expected without correlations. Our work identifies a new topological state, Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line, with CeAuAl$_3$ being the first compound explicitly identified to host this new correlated topological state, and demonstrating the expected AHE associated with it. More generally, our work outlines the pathway for finding Kondo-KNL systems in all compounds that combine achiral, non-centrosymmetric structure with Kondo correlations.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Two- and three-dimensional magnetic order in the coupled chain-ladder antiferromagnet α -Mn 3 (PO 4 ) 2
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: K. S. Chikara, A. Kumar, A. K. Bera, S. M. Yusuf
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We report a comprehensive investigation of the spin-5/2 coupled chain–ladder antiferromagnet α-Mn₃(PO₄)₂ using neutron diffraction, magnetization, optical spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The compound crystallizes in the monoclinic space group P2₁/c, forming a network of coupled chains and ladders composed of MnO₅, MnO₆, and MnO₈ polyhedra. Long-range antiferromagnetic order emerges below TN ≈ 22 with propagation vector k = (1/2, 0, 0) and an ordered moment of ~4.62 μB per Mn²⁺ at 5 K. The magnetic structure, described by the magnetic space group Pa2₁/c, consists of antiferromagnetic chains coexisting with predominantly ferromagnetic ladder correlations, consistent with DFT calculations confirming the energetic stability of the ground state. Neutron diffraction reveals a pronounced Warren-type diffuse magnetic peak in the temperature range 12 – 100 K, indicating quasi-two-dimensional short-range correlations. Reverse Monte Carlo analysis identifies dominant antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbor and ferromagnetic next-nearest-neighbor correlations, with an in-plane correlation length that decreases with increase of temperature. Notably, short-range correlations persist below TN, evidencing a gradual crossover towards three-dimensional long-range order. The magnetic phase diagram in the H-T plane, with three field-dependent regimes, has been determined. Optical spectroscopy and DFT calculations reveal a band gap of ~3.12 eV, consistent with localized Mn moments and superexchange interactions. These results establish α-Mn₃(PO₄)₂ as a model system for studying dimensional crossover and field-induced phenomena in classical high-spin coupled chain–ladder antiferromagnets.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Magnetic properties of the buckled honeycomb lattice antiferromagnet Co 3 ZnNb 2 O 9
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: A. Yadav, U. Jena, A. Pradhan, Satish Kumar, M. Pregelj, P. Khuntia
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: The intriguing interplay between competing degrees of freedom in frustrated magnets, strong electron correlations, and quantum fluctuations can lead to non-trivial magnetic phenomena with exotic low-energy excitations that are highly relevant for addressing some of the fundamental questions in quantum condensed matter as well as potential technological applications. Herein, we report the synthesis, thermodynamic results, and crystal electric field calculations on a frustrated magnet Co3ZnNb2O9. The Co2+ moments constitute buckled AB-type honeycomb layers in the ab-plane. The temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility shows a sharp anomaly at ∼ 14 K, indicating the onset of long-range antiferromagnetic ordering. The Curie-Weiss fit of the magnetic susceptibility above 100 K, yields a Curie-Weiss temperature of −70 K, suggesting strong antiferromagnetic (AFM) interactions between the Co2+ spins and an effective magnetic moment of 5.54 μB, indicating the presence of unquenched orbital angular momentum. A field-induced spin-flop–like metamagnetic transition below the ordering temperature is characterized by a critical magnetic field of ∼ 1.1 T. The specific heat shows a λ-type anomaly at 14 K, confirming the presence of long-range magnetic ordering. The long-range magnetic ordering in this magnet is ascribed to finite interlayer interactions. The observed power-law behavior of the magnetic specific heat, Cm ∼ T1.45, well below the transition temperature, suggesting the effect of intrinsic disorder in this frustrated magnet. Our results demonstrate a modest entropy change in the proximity of the transition temperature, attributed to competing interactions, magnetic anisotropy, and reduced net magnetization, highlighting frustrated honeycomb magnets as promising candidates for magnetocaloric response and perturbation induced phases.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Intertwined orders, quantum criticality, and skyrmions in tunable topological bands
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Xuepeng Wang, Johannes S. Hofmann, Debanjan Chowdhury
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Skyrmions are emergent many-body excitations that lie at the heart of both multi-component quantum Hall-like systems and deconfined quantum criticality. In a companion article (X. Wang et al., arXiv:2507.22971), we studied a microscopic time-reversal symmetric model of tunable interacting Chern bands using numerically exact determinant quantum Monte Carlo calculations, and presented evidence for the emergence of robust skyrmion excitations. These charged excitations emerge in the vicinity of a many-body insulator at a commensurate filling of the Chern bands, and lead to the onset of superconductivity when doped away from the insulating phase. Here, we present quantum Monte-Carlo results and a complementary field-theoretical analysis for the quantum phase transition(s) that arise between the intertwined phases as a function of two distinct tuning parameters. Our numerical results are consistent with a single continuous quantum phase transition between an insulating Chern antiferromagnet and a fully gapped superconductor, with an emergent SO(5) symmetry at the putative critical point, highly suggestive of deconfined quantum (pseudo-)criticality. We also present a detailed comparison between the momentum-resolved spectral functions associated with the neutral collective modes, single electron and composite spin-polaron excitations obtained using a combination of Monte-Carlo computations and a Bethe-Salpeter analysis built on top of the self-consistent Hartree-Fock calculation. We end with a brief outlook on some of the interesting open problems.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Robust Antiferromagnetic Ordering above 500 K in a Family of Bilayer van der Waals Materials
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Tengda Rong, Linxin Wu, Xingke Fu, Anqi Huang, Feiran Shen, Zixian Dong, Jianwei Huang, Hao Li, Benyuan Cheng, Lunhua He, Long Jiang, Kun Cao, Zhen Chen, Meng Wang, Xiang Chen
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Stabilizing magnetic order above room temperature in layered materials is highly desirable for low-dimensional spintronics applications. However, realizing room-temperature antiferromagnetism in layered magnets remains challenging. Here, we present a layered semiconducting oxyhalide material family, Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$ ($X$ = F, Cl, Br), which exhibits robust high-temperature antiferromagnetic ordering. The two-dimensional nature and scalability of this system are demonstrated by atomically resolving the van der Waals gap of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Br$_2$ and synthesizing centimeter-scale single crystals of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Cl$_2$. Temperature-dependent neutron scattering and magnetization measurements determine their G-type magnetic structure and transition temperature. Remarkably, the Néel temperature of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$F$_2$ ($\sim$580 K) is the highest among all reported layered antiferromagnets. Density functional theory calculations demonstrate that strong nearest-neighbor superexchange interactions along both out-of-plane and in-plane directions, particularly the magnetic couplings along lattice $c$ direction within the bilayer motif, are primarily responsible for the high Néel temperatures in Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$. In contrast, inter-bilayer spin couplings are negligibly weak, without much influence on the stabilization of the antiferromagnetic order. Therefore, theoretical calculations predict that this robust antiferromagnetic order could persist or even strengthens at room-temperature even at the monolayer limit. Our results highlight iron-based layered oxyhalides as a promising platform for exploring beyond-room-temperature antiferromagnetism in the two-dimensional limit, holding immense potential in areas like information storage and spin-based devices.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Interplay of orbital degeneracy and vacancies in stabilizing collinear magnetic order in Cr 1 + δ Te 2
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Prasanta Chowdhury, Jyotirmoy Sau, Sourav Chowdhury, Matthias Gutmann, Mohamad Numan, Soirik Dan, Amritpal, Sambit Choudhury, Sanjoy Kr. Mahatha, Jhuma Sannigrahi, Jayjit Kumar Dey, Diego Gianiolo, Moritz Hoesch, Gangadhar Das, D. T. Adroja, Saurav Giri, Manoranjan Kumar, Subham Majumdar
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Cr1+δTe2, a two-dimensional van der Waals ferromagnet, displays a contested magnetic structure, poised between collinear and non-collinear spin configurations. In this work, we elucidate the microscopic magnetic structure of Cr1.33Te2 by combining single-crystal neutron diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, angle-dependent magnetocrystalline anisotropy study, and first-principles calculations. Neutron diffraction measurements reveal a distinct collinear spin alignment, whereas spectroscopic analyses reveal inherent structural vacancies at both Cr and Te sites. These vacancies lead to local symmetry breaking that lifts the orbital degeneracy of the Cr 3d states, as demonstrated by our first-principles analysis. The resulting modification of magnetocrystalline anisotropy emerges as the key mechanism stabilising the collinear magnetic ground state over the non-collinear one in the presence of vacancies. Our findings uncover a vacancy-driven route to control spin anisotropy and magnetic ordering in layered van der Waals magnets, providing a microscopic framework for the design of tunable 2D magnetic materials.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Nonmagnetic floating phases in frustrated Haldane chains with single-ion anisotropy
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Bowy M. La Riviére, Natalia Chepiga
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We investigate the effect of a single-ion anisotropy in the bilinear–biquadratic spin-1 J 1 – J 2 chain, focusing on the quantum phase transitions out of the trimerized phase. Using large-scale density matrix renormalization group simulations, we uncover a rich phase diagram comprising five gapped phases and, remarkably, two critical floating phases. These incommensurate Luttinger liquid phases emerge from the proliferation of non-magnetic domains – S i z = 0 states and dimers – within a trimerized background and are confined to the zero-magnetization sector, while magnetic excitations remain gapped. We show that transitions between the symmetry-protected topological Haldane phase and the floating phases are governed by a composite critical line with central charge c = 2 , consistent with the coexistence of topological magnetic and non-magnetic critical modes. These results shed new light on the long-standing problem of the Haldane–trimerized transition.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Combining matrix product states and mean-field theory to capture magnetic order in quasi-one-dimensional cuprates
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Q. Staelens, D. Verraes, D. Vrancken, T. Braeckevelt, J. Haegeman, V. Van Speybroeck
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We study quasi-one-dimensional strongly correlated materials using a multi-step approach based on density functional theory, downfolding techniques, and tensor-network simulations. The downfolding procedure yields effective multiband Hubbard models that capture the competition between electron hopping and local Coulomb interactions relevant to the system's low-energy properties. The resulting multiband Hubbard models are solved using matrix product states. Applied to Sr$_2$CuO$_3$, SrBaCuO$_3$, and Ba$_2$CuO$_3$, this purely one-dimensional treatment yields no long-range magnetic order, in contrast to the magnetic ordering observed experimentally. To account for this behavior, we extend the multi-step approach by incorporating interchain couplings through a self-consistent mean-field scheme. This combined approach stabilizes finite staggered magnetizations, providing a consistent description of magnetic order in agreement with experiment. For Sr$_2$CuO$_{3.5}$ and SrCuO$_2$, we also tested an approach proposed for ladder materials, however, we find that these materials are not well suited for this approach due to the small magnitude of the intraladder hopping parameters.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Bridging Gaps with Tensor Networks: From the Haldane Gap and Beyond
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Sirui Lu
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Proofs generated by large language models are often difficult to understand, generalize, or formalize directly. Here we verify, digest, and formalize OpenAI's computer-assisted proof of a uniform gap in the periodic spin-1 Heisenberg chain using tensor-network diagrams and Lean 4. Reading the partition-function network along space and imaginary time shows how finite-ring bounds propagate across doubled lengths and inverse temperatures to all longer even rings, sharpening the spin-1 bound from the same finite inputs by a factor of 19 to $Δ_L > 0.0729$ for all even $L \geq 36$. We identify reflection positivity as the general condition behind the proof and certify uniform gaps in seven additional spin chains and ladders. More broadly, digesting machine-generated proofs into transparent physical mechanisms yields sharper bounds, broader theorems, and reusable formal verifications.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Finite-time quenches across first-, second-, and infinite-order transitions in XXZ spin chains
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Luiz Felipe Santos Dittberner, Luigi Berber, Maria C. O. Aguiar, Krissia Zawadzki, Helena Bragança
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We investigate how equilibrium quantum phase transitions manifest themselves in small systems driven out of equilibrium by quantum quenches. We consider linear ramps of the anisotropy in spin-1/2 and spin-1 XXZ chains, which host transitions of first, second, and infinite (Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless, BKT) order. We consider system sizes available in current quantum simulators and investigate how the order of the transition, the symmetries, and the ramp duration affect the decomposition of the time-evolved state into the instantaneous eigenbasis. The order of the transition determines the dynamics: across the BKT transition, moderately slow ramps already keep the system close to its ground state, corresponding to an adiabatic evolution, whereas for the second-order Haldane-Néel transition a ramp roughly three times slower is required to reach the same regime. Across the first-order transition, since the dynamics conserves the magnetization of the initial state, we observe the formation of ferromagnetic domains, separated by a single domain wall for slow ramps and by multiple walls for faster ones. Interestingly, shortly after the transition, the state evolves as a coherent beating between domain-wall states, a behavior captured by the recently proposed quantum-state texture.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Competing paramagnetic phases in the maple-leaf Heisenberg antiferromagnet
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Paul L. Ebert, Yasir Iqbal, Alexander Wietek
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We establish a remarkably rich ground state phase diagram in the maple-leaf lattice spin-$1/2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet as a function of the three symmetry-inequivalent nearest-neighbor bonds using exact diagonalization and tower-of-states analysis on clusters up to $N=36$ sites.
