Besides a hexagonal plaquette state, a star-shaped valence bond solid state is discovered in close vicinity to the (canted) $120^\circ$ magnetic phase, strongly reminiscent of a de-confined critical point or Dirac spin liquid scenario on the triangular lattice antiferromagnets. Moreover, an exact dimer product-state is observed next to a collinear Néel-state, similar to the Shastry-Sutherland model. All identified phases compete in a parameter regime close to the isotropic point, providing a promising region for spin liquids to emerge. By analyzing Gutzwiller-projected wave-functions we identify a sliver of parameter regime where a gapped $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ spin liquid Ansatz is in astonishing agreement with the exact $N=36$ ground state. This rich competition of paramagnetic phases demonstrates that the maple-leaf antiferromagnet is a promising platform for exotic states of matter and quantum critical phenomena.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: What Hall Measures in Strongly Correlated Metals
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Emily Z. Zhang, Thomas P. Devereaux
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: The Hall effect provides a sensitive probe of electronic correlations in strongly interacting metals, yet its microscopic interpretation beyond quasiparticle transport remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a Liouvillian formulation of the Hall conductivity that organizes the response into different classes of flux-sensitive many-body interference operators. Using a Schrieffer-Wolff transformation of the Hubbard model, we identify how projected charge motion and virtual hopping processes contribute to oriented trajectories enclosing magnetic flux. A high-temperature expansion reveals a hierarchy of inverse-temperature contributions associated with these interference processes. This framework provides a possible microscopic interpretation of the integer power laws previously observed in determinant quantum Monte Carlo calculations, which emerge at temperatures below the regime where the expansion is formally controlled. Our results highlight the sensitivity of Hall transport to coherent many-body dynamics and establish a connection between lattice geometry, electronic correlations, and transverse charge response.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Dimensional Crossover and Correlated Spin Dynamics in the Chain-Like van der Waals Antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: C. S. Saramgi, Y. Shemerliuk, S. Selter, S. Aswartham, B. Buechner, H. -J. Grafe, K. M. Ranjith
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We report a comprehensive investigation of the magnetic properties and spin dynamics of the chain-like van der Waals antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ using magnetization, magnetic susceptibility, and $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). The magnetic susceptibility exhibits a broad maximum near 250 K, characteristic of strong short-range antiferromagnetic correlations in a low-dimensional system. A classical Fisher-chain analysis gives an effective intrachain exchange scale $J/k_B\approx 140$ K, while a quantum $S=3/2$ nearest-neighbor-chain calculation yields $J/k_B\approx 114$ K. A constrained AF-FM zig-zag-chain calculation is also compatible with the susceptibility, supporting a dominant quasi one dimensional antiferromagnetic exchange scale of order 100 K. $^{31}$P NMR measurements provide microscopic insight into both static and dynamic spin correlations. The $K-χ$ relation displays two distinct linear regimes separated near $T^\ast\approx 250$ K, with different slopes indicating a change in the effective transferred hyperfine couplings. Below $T_{N}$, the relaxation follows $1/T_1\propto T^5$, consistent with magnon-mediated relaxation in the ordered state. The temperature dependence of the internal hyperfine field yields a critical exponent $β\approx 0.36$, consistent with three-dimensional universality. Together, these results establish AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ as a quasi-one-dimensional $S=3/2$ antiferromagnet embedded in a layered van der Waals host, in which local probes directly resolve the crossover from correlated intrachain spin dynamics to anisotropic three-dimensional magnetic order. More broadly, AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ provides a useful van der Waals platform for studying dimensional crossover, correlated spin dynamics, and hyperfine-coupling evolution in low-dimensional antiferromagnets.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Field-induced magnetic quantum phase transitions in a bilayer triangular lattice antiferromagnet K$_2$Co$_2$(HPO$_3$)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)(H$_2$O)$_2$
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Yiqiu Liu, Chengcheng Yin, Xinyu Shi, Xiaohui Bo, Kefan Du, Zhanlong Wu, Rui Bian, Shuo Li, Jun Luo, Jie Yang, Yanhong Wang, Weiqiang Yu, Rui Zhou, Jinshan Zhang, Yi Cui, Hongcheng Lu
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We present a $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study on the spin-$1/2$ bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnet K$_2$Co$_2$(HPO$_3$)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)(H$_2$O)$_2$. Measurements were performed at temperatures down to 0.06 K and magnetic fields up to 26 T. In the field range of 0.5 T to 4 T, the low-temperature spin-lattice relaxation rate $1/T_1$ exhibits a peak, signaling the onset of a magnetically ordered state. Within this ordered phase, $1/T_1$ shows gapless behavior, suggesting a spin supersolid phase. This ordering is suppressed around 4 T. Between 6 T and 18 T, clear splittings of the NMR spectra are observed, indicating the emergence of a second ordered magnetic phase. The field derivative of the low-temperature Knight shift $K_{\rm n}$ reveals changes in slope at approximately 10 T, 15.5 T, and 18 T. The first two features correspond to bulk magnetizations of $1/3$ and $2/3$ of the fully saturated moment, respectively, while the last one marks a quantum phase transition from the second ordered phase to the fully polarized state. These results establish the studied compound as a platform for investigating field-induced quantum phase transitions and emergent phases in frustrated bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnets.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Momentum-Resolved Kondo Hybridization of Nonsymmorphic Dirac-Derived Bands in CeAgBi$_2$
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Yang Luo, Hao Liu, Zhong-Tuo Fu, Qi-Yi Wu, Bo Chen, Zheng-Tai Liu, Mao Ye, Da-Wei Shen, Chen Zhang, Ying Zhou, Cun-Hui Lyu, Jin-Dong Bai, Zi-Jie Xu, Hai-Long Deng, Zhen-Xing Wu, Jun-Jie Wu, Sai-Chao Deng, Yu-Xia Duan, Jian-Qiao Meng
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: How symmetry-constrained conduction states acquire heavy-quasiparticle character is a central question in correlated quantum materials. Combining angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, Ce $4d \rightarrow 4f$ resonant photoemission, and first-principles calculations, we investigate the nonsymmorphic Kondo lattice CeAgBi$_2$. We identify quasi-two-dimensional Bi-square-net-derived bands consistent with calculated Dirac crossings and nodal lines. Resonant photoemission resolves a nearly dispersionless Ce 4$f$ band near the Fermi level, establishing Kondo heavy-quasiparticle states. Its pronounced momentum-dependent spectral weight at intersections with the identified Dirac-derived branches provides direct spectroscopic evidence for their participation in $c$-$f$ hybridization. Complementary measurements on independently cleaved samples and an effective hybridization model connect these branches to the Kondo heavy-quasiparticle spectrum. The combined results support preservation of nonsymmorphic Dirac-band connectivity under Kondo renormalization, showing how symmetry-constrained conduction states become constituents of correlated heavy quasiparticles.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Spin supersolid in triangular lattice easy-axis spin-1/2 antiferromagnet: a fermionic parton perspective
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Meng Zeng, Roderich Moessner, Shu Zhang
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: We study the supersolid order of the spin-1/2 easy-axis XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice using a fermionic parton mean-field theory built on the $π$-flux Dirac spin liquid, with the mean-field order generated by an on-site spinon interaction term and nearest-neighbor (anisotropic) spin couplings. The collective modes are obtained using the random-phase approximation (RPA). In a finite parameter region, we find the Y state as a self-consistent solution, together with the competing Y' state, which is a $90^\circ$-rotated Y state inside the order plane. The mean-field energy favors Y', even though the two states are exactly degenerate in the classical limit. However, the Y state can become lower in energy when higher-order corrections due to the fluctuations of the collective modes are considered. The Y state can also be stabilized on the mean-field level by applying small external fields, which we do in two different ways: moment-aligned local field and uniform field along the easy axis. In both cases, the RPA calculation for the stabilized Y state gives a roton minimum at the $M$ point in the excitation spectrum. A gapped pseudo-Goldstone mode above the gapless Goldstone mode is obtained as well, which has also been observed experimentally. Furthermore, we investigate the effects of tuning the spinon interaction strength and the anisotropy in spin couplings in our phenomenological model. Comparison with the recent numerical and experimental results is also discussed.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Excitonic magnetism and competing valence bond solid instabilities in $d^4$ ruthenium compounds
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Aleksandra Krajewska, Tomohiro Takayama, Hidenori Takagi
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Spin-orbit entangled $d^4$ Mott insulators serve as a rich playground for unconventional magnetism and competing quantum electronic ground states. Intra-ionic spin-orbit coupling $λ_{\rm{SOC}}$ generates a non-magnetic $J_{\rm{eff}} = 0$ singlet ground state separated from an excited $J_{\rm{eff}} = 1$ triplet. The effective intra-atomic gap $Δ_{\rm{eff}}$ between the ground state and lowest excited state is determined by $λ_{\rm{SOC}}$ and non-cubic crystal field $Δ_{\rm{cf}}$. The intersite magnetic exchange $J_{\rm{ex}}$ induces dispersion of the excited $J_{\rm{eff}} = 1$ triplet. When the triplet bandwidth $W_{\rm{t}}$ overcomes $Δ_{\rm{eff}}$, the system undergoes long-range magnetic ordering which is viewed as a condensation of spin-orbit excitons and called excitonic magnetism. In this review, we systematically survey representative $d^4$ ruthenium compounds across four distinct structural connectivities of Ru-ligand octahedra, from K$_2$RuCl$_6$ with isolated octahedra, corner-sharing perovskite Ca$_2$RuO$_4$, edge-sharing honeycombs, to corner-sharing pyrochlores, and map them onto a conceptual parameter axis of $W_{\rm{t}} / Δ_{\rm{eff}}$. We demonstrate that $d^4$ ruthenium compounds not only represent evolution from a $J_{\rm{eff}} = 0$ Mott state to excitonic magnetism but encompass a broader competition of diverse electronic phases arising from spin-orbit coupling, exchange interactions, electron hopping, crystal field and bond covalency inhabiting similar energy scales. Near excitonic quantum critical point, where $W_{\rm{t}} \sim Δ_{\rm{eff}}$, lattice geometry and chemical bonds of constituent atoms play a decisive role in selecting the electronic ground state, frequently driving valence bond solid formation that pre-empts excitonic quantum criticality.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Probing phonon-driven modulation of exchange pathways and renormalization of exchange interaction in Heisenberg antiferromagnet KNiF3
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Jayakrishnan SS, Dipanshu Bansal
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: Ultrafast control of spin dynamics is necessary for next-generation spintronic devices operating beyond conventional speed limits, but the key challenge remains to achieve selective manipulation of magnetic exchange interactions. While above-bandgap photoexcitation transiently modifies effective exchange interactions, it generally does so without mode- or pathway-selectivity, offering little to no control over which specific exchange interactions are altered. Coherent phonon excitation enables targeted modification of interatomic distances, bond angles, and orbital overlap, thereby selectively renormalizing individual exchange pathways. Here, we investigate the coherent infrared-active phonon-driven renormalization of exchange interactions and spin dispersions in the cubic fluoroperovskite KNiF3 using a Wannier projection-based Green’s function methodology, resolving both the orbital- and mode-resolved contributions to the exchange interactions. We show that different phonon modes perturb distinct atomic sites and bond angles and distances, leading to mode-dependent renormalization of exchange pathways. The mode-dependent renormalization is further accompanied by the selective lifting of degenerate exchange interactions, thereby enabling control over individual magnetic pathways. The resulting magnon renormalization quantitatively reproduces the experimentally observed two-magnon energy modulation in KNiF3. We further determine the renormalization of the phonon energy due to renormalized exchange interactions via a coupled spin-phonon Hamiltonian, finding quantitative agreement with the anomalous phonon shifts observed in spectroscopy experiments. These results establish a comprehensive microscopic picture that links coherent phonon excitation to orbital-resolved exchange interactions and spin waves renormalization.

Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.title: Magnon-Phonon-Polariton Optomechanics in a van der Waals Magnet
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.authors: Jens-Christian Drawer, Vladislav Yu. Shishkov, Bo Han, Vita Solovyeva, Iva Plutnarová, Zdeněk Sofer, Christian Schneider, Anton V. Zasedatelev, Martin Esmann
Quantum & Correlated Magnetism.abstract: The layered anti-ferromagnet CrSBr hosts self-hybridized exciton-polaritons that couple parametrically to coherent magnons and phonons. In this work, we explore the tripartite optomechanical interaction between these quasiparticles in suspended CrSBr membranes supporting high-$Q$ breathing-type acoustic phonon modes. Using resonant pump-probe spectroscopy on the polariton state, we resolve the coupled dynamics in the $\simeq 20$ GHz range while sweeping the magnon mode across the phonon resonance with an external magnetic field. We observe an attractive magnon-phonon interaction of strength $V/2π= -43$ MHz, which primarily leads to phonon amplification. At the magnon-phonon resonance, we find predominantly unidirectional energy flow from magnons to phonons while the possible back-action is limited by kinetic losses of coherent magnons. Our study enables direct interfacing of collective magnetic excitations with sound and light in layered van der Waals materials, paving the way for quantum-coherent transduction in the GHz range with optical readout.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Coherent high-velocity chiral magnons in the metallic altermagnet CrSb
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Ashutosh K. Singh, Niclas Heinsdorf, Abraham A. Mancilla, Jörn Bannies, Avishek Maity, Alexander I. Kolesnikov, Masaaki Matsuda, Matthew B. Stone, Marcel Franz, Jonathan Gaudet, Alannah M. Hallas
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Altermagnets combine the zero net magnetization of antiferromagnets with momentum-dependent spin splitting, creating new opportunities for spintronic and magnonic technologies. The full realization of this promise necessitates a material that is simultaneously metallic and altermagnetic, yet preserves the long magnon lifetimes more often seen in insulators. Here, we use polarized neutron diffraction and inelastic neutron scattering to determine the magnetic structure and spin dynamics of the metallic altermagnet CrSb. We confirm a fully compensated, collinear magnetic structure with localized Cr moments and establish the microscopic spin Hamiltonian governing its excitations. Despite its metallicity, CrSb hosts remarkably coherent magnons across its 230 meV bandwidth, with group velocities approaching 60 km/s. Along low-symmetry momentum directions, we resolve chiral magnon splitting generated by higher-order, symmetry-inequivalent exchange interactions, providing the first experimental observation of this phenomenon in a metallic altermagnet. These results reveal a nearly complete separation between magnetic and electronic degrees of freedom in CrSb and demonstrate that metallic transport, room-temperature altermagnetic order, fast coherent magnons, and chiral spin dynamics can coexist in a single material, positioning CrSb as a compelling platform for spintronic applications.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Negligible Kitaev interaction in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ revealed by neutron spectroscopy
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Hao Xu, Shufan Cheng, Yanyan Shangguan, Song Bao, Junbo Liao, Bo Zhang, Zihang Song, Shuai Dong, Maofeng Wu, Shinichi Itoh, Daichi Ueta, Jinsheng Wen
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Using time-of-flight neutron spectroscopy, we have mapped out the magnetic excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ over a broad range of energies and momenta. The observed well-defined magnon dispersions are quantitatively reproduced by linear spin-wave theory based on a minimal bilinear Hamiltonian that includes Heisenberg exchange interactions up to third-nearest neighbors, interlayer couplings, and a single-ion anisotropy term, with no need to invoke a Kitaev interaction. This finding is consistent with the fact that bromine is lighter than iodine, leading to weaker ligand-mediated spin-orbit coupling in NiBr2 than in NiI2, and consequently a reduced Kitaev interaction. Our results establish NiBr$_2$ as a Heisenberg-dominated van der Waals antiferromagnet and support the view that the ligand spin-orbit coupling governs the strength of the bond-dependent interactions within the NiX$_2$ (X = halogen) family.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Synthesis-route-dependent state selection in the frustrated spinel ZnV$_2$O$_4$
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Jem Pitcairn, Jennifer N. Graham, Jacob L. Brownlee, Shruti Chakravarty, Joya A. Cooley, Giorgia Confalonieri, A. Dominic Fortes, David W. Tam, J. Ross Stewart, Lucy Clark
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: The emergent properties of strongly correlated materials can be highly sensitive to how they are made, yet synthesis pathway is rarely treated as a fundamental variable governing their ground states. The spinel ZnV$_2$O$_4$ provides a model system in which to test this idea: its pyrochlore lattice of antiferromagnetically coupled V$^{3+}$ $S=1$ moments hosts competing spin and orbital degeneracies, while different synthesis routes yield markedly different low-temperature behaviour. Here, we show that changing the solid-state synthesis pathway reproducibly selects a distinct structural and magnetic ground state. Microwave-assisted solid-state synthesis (MASS) stabilises the cubic spinel structure to low temperature, suppressing the conventional cubic-to-tetragonal transition and preserving the highly frustrated $S=1$ pyrochlore lattice. Combining high-resolution diffraction, magnetometry and inelastic neutron scattering, we find a magnetic ground state exhibiting persistent spin-liquid-like dynamics together with partial spin freezing. Our results establish synthesis pathway as an experimental variable for selecting between competing emergent states in strongly correlated materials, revealing a route to accessing ground states not realised by conventional synthesis.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Controlled Magnon Chirality and Its Reversal by Anisotropy in Altermagnetic FeF$_2$
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: E. M. Smith, V. O. Garlea, D. Lederman, J. M. Tranquada, I. A. Zaliznyak, J. Sears
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: In altermagnets, the exchange symmetry of two mutually compensating magnetic sublattices permits spin-polarized electronic bands and chirality-split magnon bands. Because these effects have opposite signs in domains related by time reversal, magnetic-domain control is essential for their observation and utilization. Using half-polarized neutron diffraction, we demonstrate that we can control magnetic domain imbalance in a single crystal of FeF$_2$ by field cooling, and we relate this response to the established piezomagnetism in this material. Our half-polarized inelastic neutron scattering measurements directly resolve the altermagnetic splitting of chiral magnon bands. Strikingly, we observe a clear reversal of chirality near $\mathbf{Q}=(0.5,0.5,1)$, where the altermagnetic exchange splitting vanishes and no chirality is expected in a nonrelativistic exchange model. This reversal of the chirality is well explained by the presence of a transverse component of the single-ion anisotropy tensor, which rotates between Fe sublattices related by the crystal's altermagnetic $4_2$ screw symmetry. These results allow us to resolve fine features of the spin Hamiltonian for FeF$_2$ and show how symmetry-governed relativistic anisotropy can reshape altermagnetic spin dynamics, as well as providing an avenue for control of magnetic domains and the net chiral response.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: SAS_MoCa : software for small-angle scattering data analysis of large unilamellar vesicles
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Small-angle X-ray or neutron scattering (SAXS/SANS) analysis of large unilamellar vesicles (LUVs) is often limited by high-dimensional bilayer models and the lack of dedicated, statistically rigorous workflows. Here, we introduce SAS_MoCa , an open-source Python package that integrates a compositional scattering density profile (SDP) description of lipid bilayers with a separated form factor (SFF) treatment of vesicle size and polydispersity, and couples these highly parameterized models to an adaptive thermodynamic simulated annealing algorithm formulated within a constrained Bayesian framework. SAS_MoCa enables users to incorporate quantitative prior information from, e.g. , previous SAXS/SANS studies, dynamic light scattering, NMR or molecular simulations, and returns full posterior parameter distributions, uncertainties (reported as medians and median absolute deviations) and correlations even from single SAXS curves. Validation on SAXS-only data of LUVs of varying compositions demonstrates that the method yields reproducible structural parameters with uncertainties comparable to those from joint SAXS/contrast-variation SANS analyses. The modular architecture of SAS_MoCa facilitates extension to additional lipid systems and future joint SAXS/SANS or SANS-only applications.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Spin dynamics of the strongly distorted perovskite antiferromagnet LuCrO 3
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Yung-Hsiang Tung, Guochu Deng, Yinghao Zhu, Kaitong Sun, Hai-Feng Li, Shinichiro Yano
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: The study investigated the magnetic structure and spin dynamics of the orthochromite LuCrO 3 , a perovskite that adopts the GdFeO 3 -type structure. LuCrO 3 exhibits G -type antiferromagnetic ordering Γ 2 ( F x , G z ) . Inelastic neutron scattering measurements were performed on single crystals of LuCrO 3 to obtain a spin wave dispersion over the full Brillouin zone. The spin Hamiltonian includes an exchange interaction for Cr 3 + ions, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions (DMIs), and a single-ion anisotropy (SIA). The extracted exchange constants are J 1 = 1.747 (27) meV, J 2 = 1.661 (25) meV, J 3 = -0.587 (27) meV, J 4 = -0.003 (6), and J 5 = -0.473 (8). The SIA along the c axis D c = -0.034 (4) meV, and the of the DMI vectors and are determined to be = 0.160 (7) and = 0.257 (14) meV. Investigating together with a near ideal three-dimensional Heisenberg antiferromagnet LaCrO 3 , the distortion in LuCrO 3 illustrates how exchange interactions are weaken and DMIs are strengthened, giving rise to weak ferromagnetism within the GdFeO 3 -type perovskite oxide family.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Key role of orbital exchange in CoO magnetism
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Co ions in the antiferromagnetic phase of CoO are known to possess a substantial orbital moment, making this material promising for orbitronic applications. However, intersite exchange interactions involving these orbital degrees of freedom remain poorly quantified, and their role in CoO magnetism is unclear. Here, we derive a full low-energy effective Hamiltonian for CoO, including orbital exchange terms, using an ab initio force-theorem approach based on DFT+dynamical mean-field theory. We find sizable orbital interactions, with quadrupolar orbital exchange emerging as the dominant nearest-neighbor term. The collinear antiferromagnetic order obtained from the effective Hamiltonian features magnetic moments tilted away from the pseudocubic <001> direction and an orbital contribution amounting to about one-third of the total moment, in agreement with experimental estimates. We show that the moment tilting originates from the combined effect of orbital and spin-orbital exchange interactions. The same interactions also produce a prominent splitting of the lowest excitation band. By directly modeling the inelastic neutron scattering (INS) intensity, we further show that the characteristic column-like structures previously observed in CoO INS provide a clear fingerprint of orbital exchange. We also discuss possible impact of our findings for further advances in the field of complex collective excitations, their transport properties and applications in the realm of orbitronics.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: TASCopilot: A provenance-preserving assistant for triple-axis neutron scattering
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Carina Jacobson, Aditya Purohit, Srikar Kovvali, Lekhnath Poudel, Jeffrey W. Lynn, William D. Ratcliff
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Experimental decisions often depend on evidence scattered across papers, instrument logs, data files, and specialist software. A scientific assistant must connect that evidence without turning a plausible interpretation into an unsupported conclusion. TAS Co-pilot addresses this problem for triple-axis spectroscopy (TAS), which uses neutrons to probe material structure and excitations. It preserves provenance: the sources, processing steps, and review decisions behind each result. Independently maintained scientific tools communicate through structured requests and results; validation rules and human review govern how evidence can support a claim. Language models extract information and explain outcomes but do not approve scientific claims or control the instrument. Dependency-aware reduction executes existing scientific routines and reuses unchanged intermediate results. A retrospective SrMn$_2$Sb$_2$ study connects literature on a related material and historical alignment records to modeling of magnetic excitations in 20 measured scans. A live BT-7 study uses a dedicated instrument interface for fine alignment and 40 adaptively selected measurements. Agreement with a conventional measurement of the same crystal at shared conditions supports the acquisition and analysis chain. These cases demonstrate a methodology for maintaining inspectable evidence across literature, numerical analysis, and measurement at a user facility.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Coupled magnetic and lattice excitations in multiferroic Ba 3 HoRu 2 O 9 : Insights from neutron scattering, Raman spectroscopy, and machine-learned phonon calculations
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: E. Kushwaha, S. Ghosh, G. Roy, M. Kumar, M. D. Le, J. Shannigrahi, S. D. Kaushik, D. T. Adroja, T. Basu
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Inelastic neutron scattering (INS) spectra of} correlated 4 d - 4 f multiferroic oxides are difficult to interpret because magnetic, crystal-field, and lattice excitations frequently overlap in energy. The hexagonal 6H perovskite Ba 3 HoRu 2 O 9 provides an ideal platform to investigate this interplay owing to the coexistence of Ru 2 O 9 molecular units and localized Ho 3 + moments. To identify the contributions from these different excitations, we combine INS with linear spin-wave calculations, crystal-field analysis, Raman spectroscopy, and machine-learned force field (MLFF) phonon calculations. A magnetic excitation below 6.2~meV, observed only in the low-temperature magnetic phase, is reproduced by linear spin-wave theory a collective spin-wave excitation of the coupled Ru-Ho magnetic network. At higher energies, broad excitations centered near 20, 39, 70, and 90~meV are observed that persist far above the magnetic ordering temperatures. The magnetic part of the 39~meV excitation, isolated by subtracting the Bose-corrected high-temperature data, follows the Ho 3 + magnetic form factor. Crystal-field calculations based on the Stevens formalism place a group of strong Ho 3 + transitions in this energy range, while Raman spectroscopy and MLFF phonon calculations identify optical phonons with comparable energies. Together, these complementary results show that the broad INS feature near 39~meV arises from overlapping Ho 3 + crystal-field excitations and lattice vibrations. These findings establish a microscopic framework for understanding the interplay between spin, crystal-field, and lattice degrees of freedom in this multiferroic 4 d - 4 f compound.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Orbital differentiation in a rare earth ion near half filling
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: D. W. Tam, Ø. S. Fjellvåg, B. Gonano, E. X. M. Trewick, M. Månsson
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: In the electronic structure of rare earth ions, details can be crucial for understanding the origin of correlated states. Currently, state-of-the-art wavefunction-based methods (e.g. CASSCF) can capture single-ion properties of molecular magnets and some band insulating systems, but are expensive to perform, and cannot be applied to metallic systems. Here, we carry out full multiplet calculations for SmN with the cubic rock-salt structure using the crystal field software Quanty. The calculated experimental observables from our model agree precisely with magnetic susceptibility and inelastic neutron scattering experiments, and the spatially resolved spin density also agrees with DFT predictions. By tuning the crystal field parameters, our full multiplet-derived wavefunctions reveal the presence of orbital differentiation of the ground $J=\frac{5}{2}$ manifold into two groups, which are distinct subspaces with different orbital stiffness. This violation of Hund's rule, observed with a fast and inexpensive calculation tool, represents a step forward for microscopic models of rare earth materials, and may provide support for the claim of unconventional triplet superconductivity in SmN.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Zero-field magnetic structure of the antiferromagnetic intermetallic compound EuSnP
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Mizuki Urai, Hiraku Saito, Daisuke Nishio-Hamane, Taro Nakajima, Rina Takagi
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: We investigated the zero-field magnetic structure of the antiferromagnetic intermetallic compound EuSnP through single-crystal neutron diffraction experiments. The magnetic propagation vector in the magnetically ordered phase was determined to be ( 0 , 0 , 1 / 2 ) , indicating that commensurate antiferromagnetic ordering is realized in this material. The detailed magnetic structure analysis revealed a collinear A-type antiferromagnetic structure with ferromagnetic alignment of Eu 2 + moments within the Eu–P bilayer. The present findings provide a microscopic basis for understanding the intriguing magnetic behaviors of EuSnP, as exemplified by the multiple metamagnetic transitions in the antiferromagnetic state and the strong pressure dependence of the magnetic transition temperature.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Site-selective substitutions and magnetic structures in ( Fe , Co ) 2 ( P , Si ) compounds probed by x-ray linear dichroism and neutron diffraction
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: L. L. Bao, W. Wei, H. Yibole, Jiazheng Hao, Lunhua He, F. Wilhelm, A. Rogalev, F. Guillou
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: We investigate the crystallographic site occupancies and magnetic structures of ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{1.93\ensuremath{-}x}{\mathrm{Co}}_{x}{\mathrm{P}}_{1\ensuremath{-}y}{\mathrm{Si}}_{y}$ $0\ensuremath{\le}x\ensuremath{\le}0.6$ and $0\ensuremath{\le}y\ensuremath{\le}0.4$ compounds using a combined x-ray absorption/linear dichroism (XAS/XLD) and neutron powder diffraction approach. Co $K$-edge XLD, supported by fdmnes simulations, provides direct spectroscopic evidence that Co preferentially occupies the tetrahedral $3f$ site of the hexagonal ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}\mathrm{P}$-type structure. In contrast, P $K$-edge XLD and neutron diffraction show that Si is distributed over both $1b$ and $2c$ metalloid sites, with at most a weak preference for $2c$, rather than the commonly assumed exclusive $2c$ occupation. Neutron diffraction further establishes that the hexagonal ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}\mathrm{P}$-type compounds adopt a collinear ferromagnetic structure with ordered moments along the hexagonal $c$ axis, whereas the orthorhombic ${\mathrm{Co}}_{2}\mathrm{P}$-type phase observed at high Co content exhibits reduced and canted magnetic moments. Across the hexagonal series, Si substitution enhances the total magnetic moment through contributions from both $3f$ and $3g$ sites, whereas Co substitution suppresses it primarily via a reduction of the $3f$ site moment. These results provide an experimental basis for understanding why global structural parameters such as c/a alone are insufficient to rationalize the magnetic trends in ${(\mathrm{Fe},\mathrm{Co})}_{2}(\mathrm{P},\mathrm{Si})$ and demonstrate that site-selective occupancy must be included in structure-property relationships in ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}\mathrm{P}$-derived hard-magnetic materials.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Crystal and magnetic structures of MnSi in zero magnetic field: Neutron diffraction and symmetry analysis
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Vladimir Pomjakushin, Igor Plokhikh, Douglas H. Fabini, Ekaterina Pomjakushina
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Combining high-resolution wide-angle neutron powder diffraction with magnetic-superspace symmetry analysis, we refine the crystal structure and present, to our knowledge, the first systematic refinement of cubic $P2_13$ MnSi's zero-field magnetic structure across multiple magnetic satellite families. We compare single-arm rhombohedral 3+1D and cubic four-arm 3+4D magnetic superspace-group (MSSG) descriptions with propagation vectors along $\langle111\rangle$. Simultaneous extinction of the two satellite groups around $\{100\}$ dictates a transverse circular-helix model. This suppression and refinements of 18 separately varied satellite-group intensities support this ideal limit with only one adjustable magnetic amplitude. In the ideal single-arm model with MSSG $R3.1'(0,0,g)ts$, the moment has constant magnitude 0.535(3) $μ_B$ per Mn. An explicit four-arm 3+4D cubic superspace construction presented here combines four interpenetrating helices and, for the illustrated phase choice, has moments ranging from zero to 0.874(5) $μ_B$ per Mn, with the same root-mean-square moment as the 3+1D structure. Their identical powder profiles prevent the present measurements from distinguishing them. The average crystal structure remains cubic within experimental resolution, providing structural motivation for the cubic magnetic model. The mean lattice parameter, determined with formal relative precision $σ_a/a \lesssim 10^{-5}$, exhibits nonmonotonic temperature dependence below the Néel temperature.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: The physical design of the superfluid helium-4 UCN source at CSNS
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Xue-Fen Han, Bin Zhou, Song-Lin Wang, Xiao-Xiao Cai, Dong-Dong Zhou, Yi-Jie Cai, Fei Shen, Tian-Jiao Liang, Robert Golub
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Ultracold neutrons (UCN) play a crucial role in fundamental physics research, enabling investigations into new sources of CP violation, neutron lifetime measurements, and the exploration of non-Newtonian forces. However, these experiments are often limited by the intensity of UCN sources. The China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) is developing a UCN source utilizing superfluid helium-4 at Beamline 12. This paper focuses on enhancing UCN density and total UCN number by analyzing various parameters that impact the UCN system, including the influence of different wavelengths of cold neutrons, incident beam size, converter length, wall and reflector materials, extraction method, extraction guide radius, and guide material composition. A preliminary design of the UCN source at CSNS is presented based on this analysis. For a Be-coated converter, the predicted saturated UCN density is 315 UCN/cm^3, with a UCN production rate of 12,055 UCN/s and an extraction efficiency of 84%, yielding approximately 1.3 x 10^6 extracted UCNs per cycle in accumulation mode. The UCN source design presented in this study forms part of the overall physical design of the Neutron Physics and Application Spectrometer at CSNS, which successfully passed its physical design review on March 25, 2025.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Erratum: A polarized neutron study of some Co 1-x Mn x alloys by A R Wildes, S J Kennedy, L D Cussen and T J Hicks ( J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 1992 4 8961–8968)
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: A R Wildes, S J Kennedy, L D Cussen, T J Hicks
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Erratum: A polarized neutron study of some Co1-xMnx alloys by A R Wildes, S J Kennedy, L D Cussen and T J Hicks (J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 1992 4 8961–8968), Wildes, A R, Kennedy, S J, Cussen, L D, Hicks, T J

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Design of nSPIRAL: a Neutron Spectrometric Position-Weighted Radial Array Long-Counter
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: E. Mendoza, J. Guerrero-Cánovas, D. Bachiller-Perea, C. Ballesteros, D. Cano-Ott, J. García, J. Llanes Gamonoso, T. Martínez, A. Pérez de Rada Fiol, J. Plaza, L. Romero, R. Santorelli, D. Villamarín, O. Alonso-Sañudo, G. Auñón, M. J. G. Borge, J. A. Briz, F. Calviño, G. Cortés, A. De Blas, B. Fernández, L. M. Fraile, G. García, R. García, V. García-Tavora, C. Guerrero, A. Illana, N. Mont-Geli, V. Martínez-Nouvilas, E. Nácher, A. Nerio-Aguirre, M. Pallàs, A. Perea, D. Soler, J. L. Taín, A. Tarifeño-Saldivia, O. Tengblad, J. M. Udías
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: We present here the design of a neutron long counter intended to measure neutrons originating from radioactive decays or nuclear reactions. Like other similar detectors, it relies on a moderator (polyethylene) and $^{3}$He tubes. A novel feature of our design is the use of the weighting technique to achieve an efficiency that is virtually independent of the energy spectrum of the neutrons being measured; a property known as \textit{flat efficiency}. This approach offers two primary advantages: it yields a flatter efficiency response than conventional analysis methods, and it provides greater flexibility regarding the geometry of the long counter. The latter has enabled us to design the detector with almost every $^{3}$He tube positioned at a different distance from the neutron source, which allows us to perform not only neutron counting but also neutron spectroscopy.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: The microscopic origin of the hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes bundles
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Carlos Cabrillo, Ricardo Fernández-Perea, Felix Fernández-Alonso
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: In a recent study we reported large hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in samples made out of Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes (DWCNT) at supercritical temperatures (50 K, 77 K and 150 K), a physical behavior of practical interest. Here, we center our efforts in elucidate its physical origin by means of neutron diffraction (ND) and computer simulations. After a detailed theoretical modeling of the ND signal we were able to quantitatively study how the nanostructure of the material reacts to the hydrogen loads. An expansion of the bundle structure with increasing hydrogen load was found. Taking advantage of the translational symmetry of a DWCNT bundle along the nanotube axis, a two dimensional numerical analogue of the system helped us to clarify the microscopic origin of the hysteresis. Two microscopic mechanisms are identified as responsible for the metastable hydrogen adsorption, one structurally static in character, namely, H$_{2}$-load dependent effective energy barriers between interstitials, the other related to the structural deformation, namely, the opening/closing of the channels between interstitials with increasing/decreasing H$_{2}$ loads owing to the concomitant bundle expansion/contraction.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Finite temperature and pressure structural relaxations including zero-point motion and anharmonicity
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Henricus R. A. ten Eikelder, Florian Knoop, Florian Trybel
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: At finite temperature and pressure, the equilibrium structure of a crystal minimizes the Gibbs free energy rather than the static Born-Oppenheimer energy. We present WARP (Wyckoff-constrained Anharmonic Relaxations at Pressure and temperature), a symmetry-constrained, variable-cell relaxation based on the stochastic temperature-dependent effective potential method, including anharmonicity and zero-point motion. Every position update is projected onto Wyckoff positions and every strain onto symmetric strains, so a relaxation can raise the symmetry but never lower it. For aluminum, the thermal expansion follows measurements at cryogenic temperatures, including the quantum plateau below 50 K. For lanthanum hydrides at megabar pressures, equations of state agree with phonon-based and path-integral calculations, and LaH$_{10}$ relaxes from its rhombohedral static minimum to the observed cubic phase, also with a machine-learned potential fine-tuned on 150 supercells. For brucite, Mg(OD)$_2$, lattice parameters, bond distances and thermal expansion agree with neutron diffraction, and the O-D isotope effect is captured.

Neutron Scattering Techniques.title: Pair distribution function oscillations at electrostatically stabilized nanocrystal surfaces reflect nanocrystal lattice periodicity
Neutron Scattering Techniques.authors: Vivian R. K. Wall, Andrew Yang, Bryan A. Sanchez Monserrate, Ahhyun Jeong, Christian P. N. Tanner, Joshua Portner, John P. Davis, Tim B. van Driel, Burak Guzelturk, Gihan Kwon, Olaf J. Borkiewicz, David T. Limmer, Dmitri V. Talapin, Karena W. Chapman, Simon J. L. Billinge, Naomi S. Ginsberg
Neutron Scattering Techniques.abstract: Nanocrystals (NCs) stabilized electrostatically by short, multivalent inorganic ligands exhibit rich interactions and phase behavior believed to hinge on the configuration of ions at the NC surface, yet these molecular details have not previously been measured. Here we use double-difference pair distribution functions (ddPDFs) of total X-ray scattering to determine the configuration of Sn$_2$S$_6^{4-}$ ligands on PbS NCs suspended in multivalent electrolyte. The measured ddPDFs exhibit a $\sim$3-$\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ wavelength oscillation that extends $\sim$10 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$. Comparison with a PbS NC model decorated with Sn$_2$S$_6^{4-}$ ligands indicates ligands are aligned $\sim$radially, suggesting bidentate binding. Calculated partial PDFs show that the oscillatory signal is dominated by nanocrystal-Pb to ligand-Sn correlations. A simplified model that replaces the ligand with a strongly scattering Pt atom near the NC surface confirms the oscillation period in the ddPDF originates from the NC lattice constant. Nanocrystal lattice periodicity therefore merits consideration when interpreting ddPDFs of colloidal NCs.

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: Shielding design and construction for the XINGZHI cold neutron triple-axis spectrometer: integrating velocity selector, S-bender polarizer, and neutron guide
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: Hongxia Zhang, Daye Xu, Florian Grünauer, Jinchen Wang, Yuntao Liu, Juanjuan Liu, Peng Cheng, Wei Bao
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: The optimized design and construction of shielding for the velocity selector, S-bender polarizer, and neutron guide in the XINGZHI cold neutron triple-axis spectrometer have been successfully completed. The challenge of limited space available for XINGZHI has been met by a compact shielding structure, developed through Monte Carlo simulations and realized by purpose-built mechanical design, thus leaving more floor space for the spectrometer. An innovative lead-antimony alloy ensures rigidity for self-support, while optimized tolerances for gaps between mating blocks meet safety, machinability, and mounting requirements. Additionally, a long-distance alignment method has been implemented, facilitating the alternating installation of the neutron guide and shielding system. After six years of operation, this structure has been verified to meet radiation safety standards while maximizing available space, marking a significant advancement in neutron instrumentation in China and offering valuable methodologies for future development.

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: Scintillator-Based Event-Mode Neutron Imaging with Timepix4 Readout
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: Wenqin Yang, Xingfen Jiang, Junan Geng, Yang Liu, Qicai Li, Hongbin Liu, Xiaojuan Zhou, Yanfeng Wang, Li Yu, Xiuku Wang, Peixun Shen, Jiayi Ren, Yubin Zhao, Jianrong Zhou, Zhijia Sun, Yuanbo Chen
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: Scintillator-based event-mode neutron imaging is emerging as a powerful approach to neutron radiography. Unlike conventional integrating-mode neutron imaging, which accumulates scintillation light during an exposure, event reconstruction estimates neutron-event positions and arrival times from time-stamped optical responses. We investigated this approach using a self-developed Timepix4-based optical readout system, image-formation analysis, and beam experiments at the China Spallation Neutron Source under different scintillator and optical configurations. The analysis explains how event localization can reduce image blur associated with the spatial extent of individual scintillation responses. Under the same 0.35$\times$ optical configuration, event reconstruction improved the spatial resolution from 164.2 to 91.9 $μ$m at 10% modulation transfer function (MTF), while a 2.1$\times$ configuration with a $\mathrm{Gd_2O_2S:Tb}$ scintillator achieved 26.1 $μ$m at the same MTF threshold. Following event reconstruction and rejection of single-photon reconstructed events, the mean peak-normalized spectral response in the 6-8 angstrom out-of-band interval decreased by 85.4% relative to the raw-pixel wavelength-count spectrum, indicating reduced afterglow-related spectral background. Under the tested pulsed-beam conditions, the maximum instantaneous pixel-hit rate per pixel was approximately four times its time-averaged value, providing an experimental basis for assessing readout requirements at higher neutron flux. Conventional radiography resolved structural details, while energy-selective imaging enhanced the contrast between materials with similar broadband transmission and Bragg-edge imaging revealed crystallographic features in steel. These results demonstrate the imaging-quality benefits and capabilities of scintillator-based event-mode neutron imaging.

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: Development of Sapphire-Based Solid-State Neutron Detectors for Fusion Environments
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: Matteo Hakeem Kushoroa, Stephanie Cancelli, Gabriele Croci, Benno Margesin, Federica Mantegazzini, Enrico Perelli Cippo
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: Single-crystal diamond is the reference solid-state technology for fast neutron detection in fusion devices. Despite this, its complex manufacturing increases their costs and puts limitations on their geometry. Moreover, the limits in their long-term stability and their behaviour in harsh environments further constraint its applications. Synthetic sapphire (Al2O2) is a promising alternative as a solid state detector material: it is available in large, low-cost wafers and features both a wider bandgap and a higher displacement energy compared to diamond. Despite this, it has so far received little-to-no attention as a neutron detector. This work presents the first steps of a development programme for sapphire-based fast neutron detectors. Eight prototypes with 4.5 x 4.5 mm2 and 9 x 9 mm2 active areas and 625 um thickness were fabricated from commercial wafers with Al-Si electrodes and coupled to different electronic configurations. All prototypes detected 5.47 MeV alpha particles from a 241Am source, confirming the viability of both the fabrication process and the use of sapphire as an active material. The small signals (30-40 mV over a peak-to-peak noise of about 8 mV) and the count rate increasing with bias indicate that sapphires will require higher electric fields than the ones experimented in the work (up to about 2.5 kV). Geant4 simulations were also used to estimate the response of a sapphire detector to 14.06 MeV (DT) neutrons, highlighting the perspectives of the detector as a fusion diagnostic.

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: Study of neutron flux redistribution and shadowing effect in rod worth measurements with the rod drop experiment
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: Giovanni L. Stefani, Guilherme E. S. Carvalho, Daniel A. P. Palma, Marcelo V. Silva, Cesar Raitz
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: This study investigates neutron flux redistribution and the shadowing effect between control rods during rod-worth measurements using the rod-drop experiment. A simulation-based instrumental calibration methodology is proposed to account for spatial effects on neutron detector responses and improve the accuracy of reactivity measurements. The IPEN/MB-01 research reactor was modeled using the MCNP Monte Carlo neutron transport code. Reactivity behavior during the initial transient of the rod-drop experiment (t < 10 s) was evaluated and compared with experimental measurements using the source-jerk method. The methodology quantifies control rod shadowing and detector-dependent neutron flux redistribution, allowing correction factors to be established for the measured reactivity. Control-bank worth values obtained through the stable-period method were adopted as reference measurements. The reported maximum deviations from the reference values were 0.5% and 11.3%, respectively. The results demonstrate the relevance of spatial neutron flux effects, control rod interactions, and detector calibration in rod-drop experiments, providing a computational and experimental basis for improving control rod worth measurements in research reactors.

Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.title: Sub-100 meV low-energy inverse photoelectron spectroscopy using an electrostatic monochromator
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.authors: Daichi Honma, Masaya Kai, Tomoko Onishi, Taichi Suruga, Issei Ishimori, Hayato Usami, Yuki Kashimoto, Toki Shimoda, Yuto Nishimoto, Harald Ibach, F. Stefan Tautz, François C. Bocquet, Hiroyuki Yoshida
Neutron Instrumentation & Detectors.abstract: We developed a high-resolution low-energy inverse photoelectron spectroscopy (LEIPS) system by integrating a low-energy electron source equipped with a 162° electrostatic monochromator [H. Ibach et al., Rev. Sci. Instrum. 94, 043908 (2023)] into an angle-resolved LEIPS apparatus [Y. Kashimoto et al., Rev. Sci. Instrum. 94, 063903 (2023)]. Through the systematic optimization of the electron optics, pass energy, and photon detector, we achieved an overall energy resolution of 98 meV, surpassing the 0.1 eV milestone in inverse photoelectron spectroscopy. Even under throughput-optimized conditions, a resolution of 147 meV was obtained. Angle-resolved measurements on highly oriented pyrolytic graphite demonstrate its quantitative momentum-resolved capability.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Cyclotron-frequency stability via single-ion fluorescence in a Penning trap with a cryogen-free superconducting magnet
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: A. Schupeta, D. Yousaf, M. Almagro, M. Hurtado, J. M. Palomino, J. Berrocal, M. Block, Ch. E. Düllmann, D. Rodríguez
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: In this work, we investigate the magnetic-field stability of a Penning trap operated with a cryogen-free superconducting magnet through cyclotron-frequency measurements of a single laser-cooled calcium ion using two complementary photon-based detection techniques: a pulsed optical method for determining the three ion eigenfrequencies and Fluorescence-Detected Fourier-Transform Ion-Cyclotron-Resonance (FD-FT-ICR). For the former technique, the data-analysis procedure was revisited, considering it as the dominant contribution to the measurement uncertainty and yielding a long-term magnetic-field drift (1/B)(dB/dt) = −3.07(32) × 10−9 h−1. This value is comparable with those reported for high-precision Penning-trap experiments employing liquid-helium-based superconducting magnets. The short-term stability was investigated using the FD-FT-ICR technique, resulting in a minimum relative magnetic-field variation of δB/B ≃ 5 × 10−8 for averaging times between 30 and 60 s. Furthermore, this technique enables direct cyclotron-frequency determinations on timescales as short as a few seconds, providing access to magnetic-field fluctuations that are generally not resolved in conventional Penning-trap experiments.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Design and parametric modal optimization of a low-vibration liquid-helium cryostat for a cryogenic current comparator
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Jie Xie, Haiming Shao, Weibin Xi, Jipeng Fan, Qingqing Du, Changdong He
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: To meet the requirements of cryogenic current comparators (CCCs) for stable cryogenic operation in precision large direct current measurement, a low-heat-load and low-vibration liquid-helium cryostat with an external helium reliquefier was designed and optimized. The cryostat provides a 4.2 K liquid-helium bath for the CCC. To reduce disturbances from the installation environment and reliquefier, a strategy combining global low-frequency isolation and internal high-frequency vibration avoidance was adopted. The isolation layer lowers the low-order modal frequencies of the global system, while enhanced support stiffness shifts internal modes away from the main disturbance bands. Based on the available cooling capacity and measured site vibration spectra, the design criteria were defined as a 4.2 K heat load below 0.54 W, global low-order modal frequencies below 20 Hz, and an internal control modal frequency above 50 Hz. A heat-load model for the 4.2 K stage and a thermally constrained modal design window were established. With lower axial and vertical support diameters of 12 mm and 10 mm, the 4.2 K heat load is 0.53 W, and the first horizontal and vertical modal frequencies are 59.55 Hz and 69.5 Hz. With the isolation layer, the first resonance peaks in three directions are 9.7 Hz, 9.5 Hz, and 14.7 Hz. Under measured floor excitation, the one-third-octave root-mean-square velocities at the CCC remain below the Vibration Criterion C limit of 12.5 μm/s. Strength and buckling evaluations confirm sufficient safety margins under normal and fault conditions. The results provide useful design data for high-precision CCC cryostats.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Cancellation of cryocooler-induced vibration in trapped-ion systems
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Alexandra Plocki, Kyle Debry, Agustin Valdes Martinez, Isaac L. Chuang, Robert McConnell, Colin D. Bruzewicz
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: Mechanical cryocoolers offer numerous benefits for the operation of vacuum systems containing trapped atomic ions. However, the fidelity of laser-based gates can be degraded by phase noise induced by the cryocooler vibrations. We present a feed-forward vibration-cancellation system that directly measures inner shield displacement with an auxiliary interferometer and applies a compensating phase correction to the laser drive. The interferometer signal is demodulated, and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) system unwraps the displacement measurement signal, computes the required correction phase, and updates the RF drive of an in-line acousto-optic modulator (AOM) to correct for the vibration-induced dephasing. With cancellation active, the qubit coherence time improves from $3.0\pm0.4$ ms to $35\pm5$ ms, consistent with a simulation based on the measured vibration spectrum. We further validate the cancellation by artificially increasing the mechanical coupling of the cryocooler to the vacuum chamber. The vibration-induced decoherence rate is suppressed by a factor of approximately 70 at an RMS (root mean square) displacement of 0.65 $\mathrmμ$m.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: A near-quantum-limited diamond maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Morihiro Ohta, Ching-Ping Lee, Vincent P. M. Sietses, I. Kostylev, J. R. Ball, P. Moroshkin, T. Hamamoto, Y. Kobayashi, S. Onoda, T. Ohshima, J. Isoya, Hiroki Takahashi, Yuimaru Kubo
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: Current microwave quantum technologies require the amplification of weak signals with minimal added noise at millikelvin temperatures. To date, this stringent requirement has been met exclusively by superconducting technologies, such as Josephson or kinetic-inductance parametric amplifiers. A fundamentally distinct alternative approach could be offered by masers, the microwave counterpart of lasers, which were predicted as early as the 1950s to achieve quantum-limited noise performance under ideal conditions. However, their dependence on cryogenic operation historically limited further advancement. Here we demonstrate the first-ever non-superconducting, near-quantum-limited maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures utilising nitrogen impurity spins (P1 centres) in diamond. Population inversion is achieved via microwave pumping, exploiting a four-spin cross-relaxation mechanism. We realise a maximum power gain exceeding 30 dB, an added noise of approximately 2.55 quanta above the standard quantum limit, and a maximum 1 dB output compression point of −63 dBm at 6.595 GHz. The ability to operate in strong static magnetic fields of arbitrary orientation may offer a complementary, non-superconducting route for applications such as semiconducting spin-qubit readout, magnetic-resonance spectroscopy, and dark-matter axion searches.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Scattering crossover in the d -wave-like superconductor (TMTSF) 2 ClO 4 studied by specific heat measurements
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Shota Yano, Kazumi Fukushima, Katsuki Kinjo, Soichiro Yamane, Le Hong Hoàng To, Pascale Senzier, Cécile Mézière, Shamashis Sengupta, Claire A Marrache-Kikuchi, Denis Jerome, Shingo Yonezawa
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: In the quasi-one-dimensional organic unconventional superconductor (TMTSF)2ClO4, the randomness of the non-centrosymmetric ClO4 anions can be experimentally controlled by adjusting the cooling rate through the anion-ordering temperature. This feature provides a unique opportunity to study disorder effects on unconventional superconductivity in great detail. We here report on measurements of the electronic specific heat of this system, performed under various cooling rates. The evolution of the residual density of states indicates that the ClO4 randomness works as Born-limit pair breakers, which, to our knowledge, has never been clearly identified in any unconventional superconductors. Furthermore, detailed analyses suggest a peculiar crossover from strong unitarity scattering due to molecular defects toward the Born-limit weak scattering due to borders of ordered regions. This work supports the nodal d-wave-like nature of pairing in (TMTSF)2ClO4 and intends to provide an experimental basis for further developments of pair-breaking theories of unconventional superconductors where multiple electron scattering mechanisms coexist.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Anomaly to resource: The Mpemba effect in quantum thermometry
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Pritam Chattopadhyay, Jonas F. G. Santos, Avijit Misra
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: Quantum thermometry provides a key capability in temperature estimation, but most existing strategies rely on equilibrium thermometry, where the probe gets thermalized with respect to the temperature to be estimated. This equilibrium paradigm imposes intrinsic limitations: sensitivity is tied to long-time thermalization and often cannot be improved in fast, noisy, or nonstationary settings. On the other hand, the Mpemba effect, a counterintuitive phenomenon where hotter states relax faster than colder ones to a state that is colder than the other two, has mostly been viewed as a thermodynamic anomaly. Here, we establish a fundamental implication of this anomalous effect in quantum thermometry that directional Mpemba inversion is a sufficient condition that guarantees a nonequilibrium enhancement of the Fisher information for temperature estimation. Through explicit analyses of two-level and Λ-level probes coupled to bosonic baths, we show that hotter initializations can outperform both equilibrium strategies and colder initialization over a finite-time window, with a transient Fisher information enhancement of up to approximately a factor of two relative to equilibrium, realizing a metrological Mpemba effect. Our results establish that anomalous relaxation can be a general design principle for nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, enabling ultrafast and nanoscale sensing protocols that exploit, rather than avoid, nonequilibrium dynamics.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Finite-bias Coulomb blockade thermometry
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Omid Sharifi Sedeh, Christian P. Scheller, Maryam Taghilou, Henok Weldeyesus, Taras Patlatiuk, Matthias Gramich, Jukka P. Pekola, Dominik M. Zumbühl
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: Coulomb blockade thermometers (CBTs) are versatile and, in principle, primary thermometers operating down to the micro-Kelvin range but bias heating spoils the thermometry and the primary mode. Here, we introduce a method to extract the CBT electron temperature in the presence of heat created by an arbitrary bias voltage, and without assumptions on the heat flow mechanisms. The charging energy is extracted with high precision and without any other knowledge, thus making true primary thermometry possible. The experiment also reveals a subtle dependence of the charging energy on phonon temperature below 100 mK likely due to the amorphous AlO x tunnel junctions.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Numerical and experimental investigation of a high-capacity free-piston Stirling cryocooler with a parallel regenerator array: 385 W at 80 K
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Yuheng Zhang, Hangyu Ma, Guoyao Yu, Ying Ma, Haojie Sun, Shunmin Zhu, Ercang Luo

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: CHIMERA: Couette hydrodynamics for the investigation of multi-fluid extreme-Reynolds turbulence in annuli
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Pantxo Diribarne, Jérôme Chartier, Jérôme Duplat, Bernard Rousset
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: The Couette Hydrodynamics for the Investigation of Multi-fluid Extreme-Reynolds Turbulence in Annuli (CHIMERA) apparatus has been developed to investigate turbulent momentum transport in a canonical wall-driven flow using a wide variety of working fluids, from room-temperature gases to normal and superfluid helium. We present the design and characterization of a cryogenic Taylor–Couette facility in which torque is measured on a suspended outer cylinder using a torsion-pendulum sensor and a non-contact optical readout. This configuration avoids the need for cryogenic torque transducers or electrical instrumentation inside the cryostat while providing high sensitivity over a wide dynamic range. Measurements performed in gaseous helium at room temperature and in normal liquid helium reach Reynolds numbers of up to 106 and agree well with established torque correlations, validating the apparatus over more than five decades in Reynolds number. Beyond providing such an exceptionally broad operating range with a single experimental facility and a single torque sensor, the principal motivation of CHIMERA is to enable direct comparisons of turbulent momentum transport in He I and He II under identical boundary conditions. By combining the same geometry and the same global torque diagnostic in both classical and quantum fluids, the apparatus provides a unique platform for investigating how wall-driven turbulence and its scaling evolve across the superfluid transition.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Oversampled Filter Bank Channelizer for Cryogenic Detectors
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: We present the field programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of an oversampled gener- alized DFT (GDFT) filter bank, optimized for its usage in the readout of cryogenic detectors, such as the microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKID). A polyphase structure is derived underlin- ing the efficiency of complex valued subband processing, raised by a GDFT modulation. For the latter, a fast Fourier algorithm realization may be used, yielding a highly efficient polyphase imple- mentation for arbitrary integer decimation ratios. The filter bank is tested through a 16-channel GDFT channelizer. The implementation is based on the Xilinx Zynq family of FPGAs and aims to show the data reuse and flexibility offered by the GDFT channelizer structure. General design criteria are summarized for the 16-channel polyphase filter bank channelizer. The performance in hardware resource usage is also presented, taking into account one of the main objetives of the current physics experiments, aiming to have extremely large readout format.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Adaptive carrier signal synthesis for frequency-division multiplexed cryogenic detector readout
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Timo Muscheid, Benedikt Keppner, Daniel Crovo, Robert Gartmann, Marvin Fuchs, Lukas Scheller, Oliver Sander, Luis E. Ardila-Perez
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: Frequency-domain multiplexing is a fundamental technology for readout of cryogenic detector arrays on a single transmission line. Synthesizing a large number of static carrier tones for resonator stimulation eventually drives the cryogenic low-noise amplifier beyond its P1dB, introducing detector signal distortion. Scaling array sizes to O(10^6) detector pixels therefore demands minimizing the total power on the transmission line by continuous tracking of the resonances, which requires the readout electronics to be capable of updating the carrier tones dynamically. This work presents an scalable FPGA-based implementation for carrier signal synthesis based on a numerically controlled oscillator and a polyphase filter bank, enabling real-time frequency adaptivity as well as frequency resolution of 4 mHz to precisely tune the operating point, while simultaneously reducing resource usage compared to the current memory-based implementation.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: DC cryogenic modeling of open-source SkyWater 130 nm MOSFETs at 77 K using BSIM4
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: F. Beall, A. Rimal, O. Seidel, Y. Mei, A.D. McDonald, I. Parmaksiz, V.A. Chirayath, J. Asaadi, D. Braga, J.B.R. Battat
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: Cryogenic applications in high-energy physics (HEP) demand reliable, low-power CMOS electronics capable of operating at liquid nitrogen temperatures (77 K). The open-source SkyWater 130 nm (SKY130) CMOS process has previously been shown to operate at temperatures as low as 4 K making it a promising candidate for HEP applications. In this work, we characterize and model SKY130 low-threshold voltage transistors at 77 K, which is a temperature commonly used in modeling applications for liquid argon detectors. DC characteristic measurements were performed at both room temperature and liquid nitrogen temperature. We created a cryogenic modeling approach to produce a SPICE-compatible, isothermal BSIM4-based model for select transistor sizes at 77 K. The resulting model agrees with data at 77 K with an average error on the order of 20% (relative RMS). However, our models had a systematic overprediction specifically for the measured pMOS devices at the lowest measured drain bias. Due to the open-source nature of SKY130, we have made our models publicly available on Github. We hope this work will continue the trend for democratizing circuit design at cryogenic temperatures in high-energy physics by enabling open access to accurate CMOS device models at 77 K.

Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.title: Anomalous microwave response in YBa 2 Cu 3 O 7 − δ resonators beyond the two-level-system model
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.authors: Kaiwen Zheng, Nathan J. Johnson, Nathan J. Thobaben, Sidharth Duthaluru, Haochen Shen, Denae T. Cherry, David S. Wisbey, Kater W. Murch
Cryogenic Measurements & Instrumentation.abstract: We report the microwave response of coplanar-waveguide (CPW) resonators fabricated from YBa2Cu3O7−δ (YBCO) thin films over temperatures from approximately 70 mK to 40 K. The resonators exhibit internal quality factors Qi in the range of 4 × 10^3 to 10^4 at 70 mK, which increase to a maximum of approximately 8 × 10^3 to 1.2 × 10^4 near 6 K. At low temperatures, both Qi and the fractional shift of the resonance frequency ∆fr/fr increases with temperature, qualitatively resembling behavior commonly associated with two-level-system (TLS) defects. However, neither response saturates on the temperature scale set by the resonator frequency, and the loss exhibits no observable microwave-power dependence. We show that low-temperature frequency upturn may be better described by an additional paramagnetic response associated with defect-induced local moments or Andreev bound states, while the low-temperature loss follows an approximately logarithmic temperature dependence whose microscopic origin remains unresolved. These measurements establish the millikelvin performance of patterned YBCO resonators and show that their low-temperature response cannot be understood within the conventional TLS framework alone.

Scientific Instrumentation & Automation.title: Real-time data acquisition and instrumentation framework for load frequency regulation in an islanded microgrid under energy storage failures with electric vehicle impacts
Scientific Instrumentation & Automation.abstract: This research presents a real-time instrumentation and data acquisition framework for load frequency regulation (LFR) in an islanded AC Microgrid (MG). A novel cascaded FOPTID-PTID controller with a noise-resilient derivative filtering technique has been proposed. The newly developed Chaos-Based Artificial Rabbits Optimization (CARO) algorithm has been used to fine-tune the controller parameters. The suggested technique successfully reduces frequency variations brought on by measurement noise, energy storage system (ESS) malfunctions, and uncertainty in renewable energy sources (RES). Additionally, the effect of EV integration on the LFR response under ESS failures and measurement noise has been examined. Sensitivity analysis is carried out under internal parametric uncertainties to evaluate the robustness of the controller. The performance of the system is tested using MATLAB/Simulink under different operating conditions. Real-time validation has been carried out using an OPAL-RT platform. The results confirm the effectiveness and practical feasibility of the proposed instrumentation and control framework.

Thin Films & Interface Characterization.title: An automated magnetron sputtering chamber for ferroelectric thin film deposition
Thin Films & Interface Characterization.authors: Stanislav A. Udovenko, Ian Mercer, Minkyu Jung, Sarah Olandt, Ric Wilburn, Kevin Dressler, Susan Trolier-McKinstry, Jon-Paul Maria, Darren C. Pagan
Thin Films & Interface Characterization.abstract: Optimization of next-generation materials synthesis and manufacturing processes can be accelerated by effective use of digital datasets. However, a majority of existing custom research infrastructure, including that for thin film deposition, is primarily manually operated and not compatible with this new research paradigm. Here, a template is provided for upgrading existing manual deposition chambers to enable automated and autonomous experimentation. As an example, the upgrade of an existing magnetron sputtering chamber dedicated to the synthesis of wurtzite ferroelectrics is presented. Focus is placed on automation of instrumentation; system and deposition control; and synchronized and automated data collection strategies. An example use case of the system for semi-autonomous determination of processing–property relationships is presented, specifically, minimization of the coercive field in wurtzite Al1−x−yScxByN thin films.

Thin Films & Interface Characterization.title: Data-driven reassessment of lattice matching in ScAlN/GaN heterostructures grown by sputter epitaxy and molecular beam epitaxy
Thin Films & Interface Characterization.authors: Atsushi Kobayashi, Takuya Maeda, Thai-Son Nguyen, Huili Grace Xing, Debdeep Jena, Yoshio Honda
Thin Films & Interface Characterization.abstract: We reassessed the lattice-matching behavior of ScAlN thin films grown on GaN by constructing a unified dataset from sputter epitaxy, molecular beam epitaxy (MBE), and literature reports. The dataset comprised 197 samples, including 32 MBE-grown and 70 sputter-grown films from our laboratories and 95 literature data points, for which Sc composition, growth temperature, film thickness, polarity, growth technique, and a- and c-axis lattice constants were compiled. The compiled data were analyzed using a neural-network-based surrogate model to extract smooth lattice-constant trends within the experimentally covered parameter range, and these trends were subsequently parameterized by empirical polynomial functions of Sc composition and growth temperature. The lattice-matched Sc composition of ScxAl1−xN to GaN was estimated to be x ≈ 0.10–0.13, which is lower than the conventional value of approximately 0.18 and is only weakly dependent on growth temperature and growth technique. In contrast, the c-axis lattice constant was strongly dependent on growth temperature and decreased at higher growth temperatures. This c-axis contraction, together with the reduced c/a ratio, is consistent with growth-temperature-dependent bond softening and local structural distortion in ScAlN, providing a possible structural link to polarization switching in ferroelectric nitrides.

Thin Films & Interface Characterization.title: Kinetic arrest of a disordered first-order phase transition in strained V 2 O 3 thin films
Thin Films & Interface Characterization.authors: Sindhunil Barman Roy
Thin Films & Interface Characterization.abstract: We develop a continuum phenomenological theory for the kinetic arrest (KA) of a first-order phase transition, taking the thermal and electric field-driven metal–insulator transition in epitaxial V 2 O 3 thin films as a prototype. By defining a coarse-grained mesoscopic order parameter ϕ ( r , t ) ≡ 1 − θ ( r , t ) / θ 0 representing the metallic volume fraction coupled to the primary structural monoclinic distortion θ , we formulate a Time-Dependent Ginzburg–Landau framework integrated with a non-local elastic interaction kernel and an Imry–Wortis quenched disorder landscape. We derive an explicit dynamic criterion for the KA boundary T K ( E ) by analyzing the divergence of the intrinsic order-parameter relaxation time relative to experimental observation timescales. Our framework rigorously decouples the thermodynamic driving force from the kinetic activation barrier. We demonstrate that epitaxial substrate-induced clamping elevates local elastic barriers, pinning domain boundaries and stabilizing an arrested, inhomogeneous mosaic of metallic and insulating phases down to cryogenic temperatures. The simulated transformation kinetics exhibit an Avrami exponent suppression to values n < 1 , reflecting slow, hindered domain-wall propagation. Furthermore, we examine the effect of an external electric field as an isothermal mechanism that lowers this kinetic barrier, providing a phenomenological description of threshold de-arrest and multi-level resistance states. We critically discuss this electronic barrier-lowering mechanism in comparison with electrothermal Joule heating, establish diagnostic criteria to distinguish them, and contextualize these non-equilibrium dynamics with related phenomena in disordered superconducting films.

Thin Films & Interface Characterization.title: Influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and periodicity on giant chiral asymmetry of domain wall mobility in epitaxial Cu/Pd/Co/Pd(111) films
Thin Films & Interface Characterization.authors: N. N. Chernousov, A. S. Pashenko, A. G. Kozlov, A. A. Turpak, A. S. Samardak, A. V. Davydenko
Thin Films & Interface Characterization.abstract: We investigate the influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity on the chirality-dependent mobility of domain walls (DWs) in epitaxial Si(111)/Cu(2-7 nm)/Pd(3 nm)/Co(0.7 nm)/Pd(3 nm) heterostructures. By varying the Cu buffer layer thickness, we systematically modify the morphology of the magnetic interfaces while maintaining a constant composition and thickness of the Pd/Co/Pd trilayer. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals that increasing the Cu thickness leads to the development of a hierarchical interfacial morphology characterized by increasing roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity. We observe a dramatic enhancement of the asymmetry between the velocities of DWs with opposite chirality in the creep regime, reaching a velocity ratio of approximately 50000 in the sample with a 7-nm-thick Cu buffer layer. This value exceeds by more than an order of magnitude the effective saturated asymmetry previously observed in Pd/Co/Pd structures with roughness controlled by the bottom Pd layer thickness.
