Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: The present work reports the effects of 120 MeV Au^{+} swift heavy ion (SHI) beam irradiation on the structural and magnetic properties of [Gd/Co] multilayers. Intermixing at the interfaces is observed with synchrotron x-ray reflectivity measurements with increasing irradiation fluence. As a consequence, the magnetic properties of the [Gd/Co] system are modified significantly. Detailed temperature dependent magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) measurements reveal that the SHI beam irradiation results in (i) the development of an in-plane magnetic anisotropy (ii) the increase of the magnetic compensation temperature (T_{Comp}) and (iii) signatures of spin-flop non-collinear phases at higher fields and their tuning. Linear variation of T_{Comp} is observed with irradiation fluence, reaching a value of about 500 K, the maximum reported such value in the literature. Further, the signatures of surface / bulk twisted magnetic phases are observed from MOKE and bulk magnetization measurements. All these experimental observations are explained with molecular dynamics simulations and it is shown that the intermixed GdCo alloy layer spin configuration play a dominant role in enhancing the T_{Comp}.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Tunable coupling between valley and magnetic excitons in WS2/CrSBr heterostructures
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Jianchen Dang, Liza Godziashvili, Kaichen Xie, Arun Ramanathan, Vadym Kulichenko, Alejandro Busto, Jia-Yi Ji, Robert Boyd, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Sina Najmaei, Daniel Rhodes, Luis Balicas, Xavier Roy, Ting Cao, Xiao-Xiao Zhang
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Interfacial coupling in van der Waals two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offers an effective route to tailor the electronic, optical, and magnetic properties of materials. Versatile control and precise engineering of such interlayer interactions can be further achieved through external parameters, like electric field, magnetic field, optical excitation, as well as layer stacking geometries. Here, we examined the magneto-optical properties of 2D semiconductor heterostructures made of antiferromagnetic CrSBr and a monolayer WS2, both of which host intriguing excitonic properties. We identified a type-II band alignment between these two layers and the magnetic proximity effects from CrSBr, manifested by an enhanced Zeeman valley splitting in the WS2 layer. The interlayer charge transfer shows strong spin selectivity and is governed by the relative alignment between the valley-spin polarization of photoexcited carriers in WS2 and the magnetization in CrSBr, giving rise to spin-sensitive circularly polarized photoluminescence (PL) from WS2. Furthermore, the highly anisotropic electronic dispersion in CrSBr enables stacking-dependent control of interlayer interactions, as inferred from a twist-angle dependence of PL quenching. Our work establishes a highly tunable 2D system that integrates valleytronics and magnetic excitons through multiple coupling channels, opening up new opportunities in all-optical manipulation of spin and magnon states and for the development of flexible spin-optoelectronic devices.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: High-bandwidth heterodyne sensing with bulk N- V diamond
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: H. A. M. Taylor, J. P. Duff, L. B. Miller, A. Tritt, M. S. Oldfield, K. Helmerson, M. S. J. Barson
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Developing high performance portable sensors is of significant importance for both terrestrial and satellite communications, with quantum sensors offering potential advantages in sensitivity and bandwidth. The nitrogen vacancy center in diamond is a popular quantum sensing platform for its relative simplicity and wide range of acceptable operating conditions, but suffers a limited instantaneous bandwidth due to the narrow linewidth of the spin resonance. In this work, we first present a magnetic quantum sensing scheme utilizing heterodyne mixing with strong optical and microwave driving, achieving MHz-scale instantaneous bandwidth and with a sensitivity of 548 pT/√Hz in a diamond volume of 2.5×10[−][4] mm[3] with 2×10[11] NV centers. We then demonstrate expansion of the sensing bandwidth by employing a strong magnetic gradient and individually modulated microwave control fields, expanding the single resonance FWHM bandwidth to 48 MHz with a peak sensitivity of 8.5 nT/ √Hz.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Decoherence-resilient distributed quantum sensing beyond the standard quantum limit
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Dong-Hyun Kim, Ilhwan Kim, Yosep Kim, Seongjin Hong, Yong-Su Kim, Kwang Jo Lee, Changhyoup Lee, Hyang-Tag Lim
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Distributed quantum sensing exploits entangled states to estimate global functions of physical quantities with enhanced sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit (SQL). In practice, however, unavoidable decoherence degrades quantum coherence and can lead to sensitivities lower than those of classical strategies. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a noise-robust distributed quantum sensing protocol that employs local unitary operations to maintain enhancement beyond the SQL under dephasing. Using a four-photon Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger state with the local Hadamard operations, we estimate the average of four phases distributed across four nodes via 7 km of optical fiber in a dephasing environment and observe enhancements from 1.72 ± 0.29 dB to 3.01±0.17 dB over the SQL. Our results establish a practical route to decoherence-resilient quantum sensor networks with currently available entangled resources.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Thermodynamic signatures of a nearby quantum critical endpoint in UTe$_2$ under intense magnetic field
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: M. Gen, K. Somesh, A. Miyake, D. Li, Z. Yang, A. Miyata, Y. Kohama, M. Kondo, M. Tokunaga, D. Aoki, W. Knafo
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Several unconventional superconducting phases have been discovered in the vicinity of metamagnetism in the heavy-fermion paramagnet UTe$_2$ under magnetic field. To describe the mechanism of magnetic-field-induced superconductivity, a challenge is to characterize the quantum critical magnetic properties at the metamagnetic transition. In this work, we investigate the thermodynamic properties of UTe$_2$ under magnetic fields up to 60~T applied in the crystallographic $\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{c}$ plane. Magnetization and magnetostriction experiments have been performed under magnetic fields tilted by an angle $θ\lesssim42^\circ$ from $\mathbf{b}$ toward $\mathbf{c}$. They support that a quantum critical endpoint at the field angle $θ_{QCEP}\simeq(70\pm10)^\circ$ and magnetic field $μ_0H_{QCEP}\simeq(75\pm10)$~T terminates the metamagnetic transition line. A pseudo-gap in the magnetic susceptibility is related with the metamagnetic transition observed in magnetic fields for $θ<θ_{QCEP}$. The possible relation between the quantum critical endpoint and the development of magnetic-field-induced superconductivity is discussed.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: 5/9-magnetization plateau and possible spin supersolidity in ${\rm YCu_3(OD)_7xBr_{2+x}}$ under magnetic fields up to 120 T
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Hiroaki Hayashi, Han Li, Feng-Feng Song, Xu-Guang Zhou, Akira Matsuo, Taeyun Kim, Enze Lv, Yuto Ishii, Zhe Qu, Gang Su, Koichi Kindo, Kwang-Yong Choi, Wei Li, Yasuhiro H. Matsuda
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: We performed high-precision magnetization measurements up to 120~T on three compositions of the newly discovered kagome antiferromagnet YCu 3 (OD) 7 − x Br 2 + x (YCOB), revealing a previously unobserved 5/9 fractional magnetization plateau. All YCOB samples with different Br − concentrations exhibit nearly identical magnetization curves below 60~T, whereas the 5/9 plateau appears at markedly different fields in the ultrahigh-field regime. By modeling the experimental data using tensor-network calculations, we derive the effective spin Hamiltonians for the YCOB family with three spatially anisotropic Heisenberg couplings (the 3 J -type model), which quantitatively reproduces the measured magnetization processes and captures the composition-dependent evolution of the 5/9 plateau. Furthermore, our theoretical analysis suggests the emergence of a spin supersolid phase in the field window between the 1/3 and 5/9 plateaus, whose sensitivity to spin exchange parameters accounts for the significant variation in the critical fields of the 5/9 plateau observed among different YCOB compositions.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: In-plane orbital magnetization with layer hybridization
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Jin-Xin Hu, Zi-Ting Sun, Yugui Yao
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: The modern theory of orbital magnetization successfully describes the response of Bloch electrons to magnetic fields in fully periodic crystals, but it does not directly address the distinct regime of an in-plane field in multilayer systems with layer hybridization. Coherent interlayer tunneling allows electrons to form circulating current loops, producing an in-plane orbital response that is absent in strictly two-dimensional limit and qualitatively different from the conventional three-dimensional one. Here we develop a theory of in-plane orbital magnetization for this {} regime, where the layer thickness is comparable to the vertical mean free path. Starting from the current-loop picture, we construct the in-plane orbital angular momentum operator and derive exact expressions for the orbital magnetic moment and the in-plane orbital magnetic susceptibility. As a concrete physical application, we predict a gate-tunable in-plane orbital magnetoelectric effect in layered materials. Our framework establishes a general foundation for in-plane orbital responses and suggests new opportunities for orbitronics in layer-hybridized quantum materials.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Tailored magnetic domain-wall ratchet effects through density gradients in triangular-hole arrays
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Julia Herrero-Albillos, María Ángeles Laguna-Marco, María Vélez, Xabier Zubizarreta-Iriarte, Daniel Arechavaleta, Aurelio Hierro-Rodriguez, Carlos Quirós, Michael Foerster, Cristina Bran, Arantxa Fraile-Rodriguez, José Ignacio Martín
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: We investigate domain wall (DW) dynamics and morphology in amorphous Co$_{0.86}$Zr$_{0.14}$ thin films patterned with engineered, density-graded triangular-hole arrays. Using Kerr microscopy and high-resolution XMCD-PEEM imaging, we demonstrate that DW propagation is governed by the interplay between hole orientation, density gradients, and local magnetostatic interactions. In cooperative configurations, the density gradient reinforces the geometric ratchet effect, whereas in competing configurations, the two mechanisms oppose each other, leading to an inverse ratchet and enabling experimental access to backward DW propagation. Remarkably, density-graded arrays substantially reduce the stochastic variability of depinning fields observed in periodic arrays, resulting in highly reproducible DW motion. The depinning fields are described by a rigid DW model and an empirical scaling law incorporating both inter-hole spacing and array periodicity. These results demonstrate that engineered density gradients provide an effective route to deterministic control of DW propagation, with potential applications in spintronic and neuromorphic devices.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Interplay of Ni Order and Local Moments in Intercalated NixNbS2
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Gaurav Pransu, Naveen Singh Dhami, Wojciech Sas, Yuki Utsumi Boucher, Bruno Gudac, Ana Smontara, Davor Tolj, Victor Balédent, Mario Novak, Neven Barišić, Ivo Batistić, Mirta Herak, Petar Popčević
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Magnetic ions intercalated into the van der Waals gaps of layered transition metal dichalcogenides provide a system where local moments interact strongly with a metallic host. How the order of the intercalant sublattice affects their magnetism is important but rarely addressed, although disorder is hard to avoid, in particular in thin films and heterostructures. Here this question is examined in single crystals of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ with $0.10 \leq x \leq 0.57$, whose composition and Ni order were determined by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy and synchrotron x-ray diffraction. Anisotropic magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal three regimes. Long-range antiferromagnetic order appears only for $0.25 \leq x \leq 0.33$, where the Ni ions form the $2 \times 2$ and $\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3}$ R$30^\circ$ superstructures, and $T_\mathrm{N}$ reaches 96 K at $x = 1/3$. In this range the effective moment, $\approx 2.5 μ_\mathrm{B}$ per Ni, agrees with DFT+$U$ calculations, in which the Ni spin is partly delocalized onto the surrounding S ligands. For $x \leq 0.18$ the dilute, randomly distributed Ni ions remain paramagnetic down to 2 K with a reduced moment. For $x \geq 0.37$, where Ni-Ni contacts are unavoidable, long-range order gives way to a short-range ordered state below 10-15 K with a further reduced moment. As calculations for ordered Ni arrangements find the Ni state nearly independent of $x$, even at $x = 1/2$, the reduction of the moment is attributed to a disorder-enabled reduction of the charge transfer from Ni to the NbS$_2$ layers. The magnetism of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ is thus governed by the (dis)order of the Ni sublattice rather than by the Ni concentration alone.

Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.title: Quantum sensing-enabled deuterium NMR spectroscopy with nanoscale sensitivity at low magnetic fields
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.authors: Dileep Singh, Riley W. Hooper, Christoph Findler, Utsab Banerjee, Dominik B. Bucher
Quantum Sensing & Magnetic Characterizat.abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unparalleled access to molecular structure and dynamics but is traditionally limited by weak signal strength, requiring large sample volumes and high magnetic fields. Here, we demonstrate nanoscale deuterium ( 2 H) NMR spectroscopy using nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, yielding characteristic quadrupolar powder line shapes that are present in conventional bulk NMR spectra. By detecting statistical spin fluctuations from nanometer-scale detection volumes, our approach delivers a sensitivity enhancement of seven to eight orders of magnitude in terms of spin sensitivity over inductive detection, while operating at magnetic fields two orders of magnitude lower than those used in conventional NMR. Temperature-dependent measurements of a deuterated polymer and a molecular solid reveal distinct motional averaging and phase transitions with nanoscale sensitivity. Powder-like NV-detected 2 H NMR establishes a powerful tool for probing molecular dynamics on the nanoscale - capabilities beyond those of most existing spectroscopic techniques.

Topological Materials.title: Tunable giant anomalous Hall effect in bilayer magnetic topological insulator
Topological Materials.authors: Basavaraja G, Mukul Kabir
Topological Materials.abstract: In the two-dimensional limit, the intrinsic magnetic topological insulator MnBi 2 Te 4 offers an exceptional platform for probing novel quantum states and their response to external perturbations. Using first-principles calculations and classical Heisenberg Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that electrostatic gating and surface chemical functionalization trigger a remarkable crossover from the topological to the conventional anomalous Hall regime. This transition is governed by the simultaneous shift of the Fermi level and an antiferromagnetic-to-ferromagnetic reversal of interlayer coupling. Notably, hole doping drives the Fermi level deep into the valence bands, unlocking Berry curvature hot spots that generate an exceptionally high anomalous Hall conductivity of 1380 S/cm. Conversely, surface chemical functionalization preserves a Chern band manifold coexisting with metallic states, where intrinsic σ xy is reduced from e 2 /h to ∼ 0.86 e 2 /h due to the spectral coexistence of a chiral edge mode with the metallic bulk states of the two-dimensional film. Critically, both tuning strategies significantly strengthen in-plane exchange interactions, driving a substantial increase in the magnetic ordering temperature compared to the pristine bilayer. These findings establish a powerful, versatile strategy to concurrently tailor the topological, magnetic, and transport properties of ultrathin MnBi 2 Te 4 , advancing the design of reconfigurable quantum devices.

Topological Materials.title: Magnetism of monolayers of the van der Waals semiconductors FeCl 2 and FeBr 2 epitaxially grown on Bi 2 Se 3
Topological Materials.authors: Sebastien E. Hadjadj, Mihovil Bosnar, Andrea Aguirre-Baños, Samuel Kerschbaumer, Danilo Longo, Weibin Li, Pierluigi Gargiani, Ilya I. Klimovskikh, Matthias Muntwiler, Cinthia Piamonteze, Jakub Regner, Zdenek Sofer, Amitayush Jha Thakur, Oleksandr Stetsovych, Wolfgang Kuch, Jorge Lobo-Checa, Pavel Jelínek, Fernando Delgado, Maxim Ilyn, Andres Arnau, Celia Rogero
Topological Materials.abstract: Magnetic van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures combining topological insulators (TIs) with low-dimensional magnetic semiconductors hold promise for novel quantum and spintronic phenomena where magnetic proximity effects can break time-reversal symmetry and open a gap in the Dirac surface states, a key signature enabling phenomena such as the quantum anomalous Hall effect. However, recent studies of transition metal dihalide (TMDH) monolayers on have reported the absence of such a gap, raising fundamental questions about the nature of magnetic proximity coupling in these heterostructures. Here, we demonstrate robust ferromagnetic ordering down to the monolayer limit in epitaxial and on , thereby ruling out the absence of magnetism as the origin of the missing Dirac gap. We further identify distinct magnetic ground states exhibiting out-of-plane ferromagnetism in . For , the normal incidence (NI) and grazing incidence (GI) XMCD and magnetization curve measurements reveal only weak magnetic anisotropy. Combined temperature- and field-dependent magnetisation measurements, along with Arrott-plot analysis, support a potential non-collinear ferromagnetic ground state. However, the precise magnetic structure cannot be reliably determined from the current data, since the X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) measurements were only performed in the NI and GI geometries. These findings change the interpretation of magnetic proximity effects, indicating that the absence of a gap arises instead from weak interlayer (TMDH/TI) exchange coupling. Complementary density functional theory (DFT), multiplet calculations and simulations permit us to explain the observed magnetic moment values. Our findings establish the systems / and / as a new platform to explore the interplay between magnetic proximity effects and moiré-induced modifications of topological surface states.

Topological Materials.title: Magnetization-free quantum anomalous Hall effect in altermagnetic weak topological insulators
Topological Materials.authors: Yanmiao Han, Yu-Hao Wan, Peng-Yi Liu, Rundong Zhao, Qing-Feng Sun
Topological Materials.abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect is usually realized through ferromagnetism or magnetic dop ing, which limits material choices and often results in low mobility, disorder sensitivity, and low operating temperatures. Here, we propose a mechanism to achieve the QAH phase without net magnetization, using altermagnetic exchange on a weak topological insulator (WTI). The altermagnetic order selectively gaps the Dirac cone at the Z point, while hybridization between the top and bottom surfaces of the WTI thin film opens a trivial gap at the point, generating a Chern number C = 1 phase with a single chiral edge channel. We verify the topological transition through both a minimal thin-film model and a slab geometry, and compute the associated Hall response. As altermagnets and layered WTIs already exist experimentally, this mechanism offers a promising and experimentally accessible route to realizing QAH phases without magnetic doping or global magnetization. The results indicate that altermagnetic surface engineering may provide a clean and controllable pathway for realizing dissipationless edge transport in layered quantum materials.

Topological Materials.title: Half-integer quantum anomalous Hall effect in MnBi 2 Te 4 via nonmagnetic extension
Topological Materials.authors: Igor P. Rusinov, Tatiana V. Menshchikova, Evgueni V. Chulkov
Topological Materials.abstract: Within an ab-initio approach, we study the electronic structure and Hall response of the antiferromagnetic topological insulator film of MnBi 2 Te 4 in contact with non-magnetic GeBi 2 Te 4 (Bi 2 Te 3 ) overlayer. The proposed junction design eliminates the exchange splitting one of the Dirac cones of the MnBi 2 Te 4 (0001) thus manifesting a half-integer quantum anomalous Hall phase. The described recipe allows to enlarge temperature of the effect observation, enriches the diversity of topological properties of the MnBi 2 Te 4 compound and is appropriate for other layered antiferromagnetic topological insulators. Applying the proposed heterostructure design, the half-quantized Hall phase can be established with employing other overlayer and magnetic topological insulator films.

Topological Materials.title: Topological magnons and large orbital Nernst effect in a zigzag Kitaev antiferromagnet
Topological Materials.authors: Shreya Debnath, Saurabh Basu
Topological Materials.abstract: The exploration of topological and transport properties of collinear antiferromagnets and the role of Kitaev interactions in realising topological states therein have rarely been systematically addressed in literature. In this context, we consider a zigzag-ordered antiferromagnet with both extended Kitaev and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions (DMI) in presence of an external magnetic field to focus on the topological magnons and study their transport properties. The hybridization between the up- and down-spin sectors induces opening of a bulk gap in the band structure, giving rise to nontrivial topological phases characterized by a finite Chern number, chiral edge modes, and a nonzero thermal Hall conductivity, through which different topological phases are distinctly identified. Furthermore, generally speaking, even when the net spin moment vanishes, a finite magnon orbital moment may still persist to yield a finite Nernst response owing to spin and orbital magnetization having distinct origin. This motivates us to investigate the orbital moment of the magnons, the corresponding orbital Berry curvature and the orbital Nernst conductivity. A large orbital Nernst conductivity is noted in the absence of an external magnetic field, that may hold key to intrinsic orbitronic applications. For completeness, we briefly discuss the scenario corresponding to a N'eel-type spin ordering, which leads to a vanishing Chern number, along with suppressed thermal Hall and orbital Nernst conductivities compared to the zigzag-ordered case.

Topological Materials.title: Multiple electronic phase transitions in room-temperature second-order topological insulator
Topological Materials.authors: Chaosheng Hao, Fei Wang, Li Deng, Hanghui Li, Xianmin Zhang
Topological Materials.abstract: Two-dimensional magnetic materials with coupled valley and topological properties provide an attractive platform for next-generation spintronic and valleytronic applications. Here, using first-principles calculations, the novel monolayer SeVPH is predicted as a dynamically, thermally, and mechanically stable magnetic semiconductor. Its Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless transition temperature is 382 K. Spin–orbit coupling generates a valley splitting of 68 meV in the valence band with magnetization oriented along the +z direction, resulting in the anomalous valley Hall effect. Moreover, the monolayer SeVPH is identified as a second-order topological insulator (SOTI) hosting robust corner states. Biaxial tensile strain modulates the valley degree of freedom to induce successive topological phase transitions, driving the system from the SOTI to valley-polarized quantum anomalous Hall phase and then to a trivial normal insulator. These findings demonstrate that monolayer SeVPH is a promising multifunctional quantum material for tunable ferrovalley, spintronic, and topological devices.

Topological Materials.title: Spin-resolved nodal line, spin-orbit-coupling-induced Weyl points, and associated intrinsic spin-Hall response in altermagnetic Mn 2 (PO 4 )O
Topological Materials.authors: Xiang-Feng Yang, Jun-Tao Ma, Kai-Yuan Zhang, Hua-Hua Fu
Topological Materials.abstract: Altermagnets exhibit compensated collinear magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, attracting interest for spintronic applications. Here, using first-principles calculations and symmetry analysis, we identify Mn 2 (PO 4 )O with spin group F − 1 d 1 d − 1 d ∞ m 1 as an altermagnet hosting nodal-line and Weyl physics. In the absence of spin-orbit coupling (SOC), its spin-resolved band structure hosts glide-mirror-protected spin-resolved nodal lines that extend through the periodic Brillouin zone and form a geometrically closed arrangement within the first Brillouin zone under altermagnetic order; each line continues within its own spin sector, so this closure does not imply spin switching at the high-symmetry junctions. It also hosts four nodal arcs protected by an effective antiunitary symmetry acting within each spin sector, with the spin-up and spin-down arcs arranged alternately in momentum space. The individual spin-resolved nodal lines in both spin channels carry a quantized Berry phase of π modulo 2 π , reflecting their local topology. Including SOC reconstructs these structures: the glide-mirror-protected lines leave five pairs of Weyl points (WPs), the high-symmetry spin-degenerate lines leave four additional pairs, and the effective-symmetry-protected arcs become fully gapped. The resulting WPs and gapped remnants are accompanied by pronounced spin Berry-curvature hot spots and intrinsic spin Hall conductivity, with the spin-resolved arrangement providing the underlying band framework rather than a separate enhancement mechanism. The conductivity tensor satisfies σ x z y = - σ y z x as constrained by glide-mirror symmetry. Our results establish Mn 2 (PO 4 )O as a material platform for exploring the interplay between altermagnetism, nodal-line topology, and Weyl physics, and for a chemical-potential-dependent intrinsic spin Hall response.

Topological Materials.title: Topological magnonic black-white hole crystal
Topological Materials.authors: David Galvez-Poblete, Rubén M. Otxoa, Alvaro S. Nunez, Sebastian Allende
Topological Materials.abstract: The low-energy dynamics of antiferromagnetic spin waves map onto a massive Klein-Gordon scalar field, providing a solid-state platform for analogue-horizon physics. We show that an inhomogeneous spin current generates an effective magnon flow capable of forming black- and white-hole horizons. Horizon-pair cavities exhibit resonant transport and superradiant-like amplification mediated by magnon-antimagnon mixing. Our central result is that a periodic arrangement of submagnonic and supermagnonic regions forms a non-reciprocal magnonic crystal in which entering the supermagnonic regime makes negative-norm propagating channels available and enables the bulk gap to close and reopen. This drives a topological transition characterized by a change in the Zak phase and the emergence of a hybrid magnon-antimagnon edge state. These results establish a direct connection between analogue-horizon physics and topological magnonics, providing an electrically tunable route for controlling magnonic band topology.

Topological Materials.title: Intertwined Spin Chirality and Weyl Topology Driven Giant Hall Responses in Nd$_{4}$Sb$_3$
Topological Materials.authors: Anu, Subhasmita Kar, Bhagyashree Pol, Debarghya Dutta, Aftab Alam, P D Babu
Topological Materials.abstract: Magnetic Weyl materials offer a unique platform for coupling magnetic order with real- and momentum-space topology, yet their simultaneous manifestation in a single material remains uncommon. Here, Nd$_4$Sb$_3$ is established as a highly spin-polarized magnetic Weyl semimetal exhibiting intertwined anomalous and topological Hall responses. Nd$_4$Sb$_3$ orders ferromagnetically below $T_{\mathrm{C}}\sim72$ K and undergoes spin reorientation near 42 K into a non-coplanar magnetic state. A large topological Hall resistivity of $\sim3.9 μΩ$ cm and anomalous Hall conductivity reaching $\sim1170$ S cm$^{-1}$ are observed. First-principles calculations identify an energetically preferred non-coplanar state with finite local scalar spin chirality, providing a microscopic route to the real-space Berry phase underlying the topological Hall effect. Calculated exchange interactions reveal dominant ferromagnetic exchange together with anisotropic exchange and finite Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions, while Monte Carlo simulations yield a magnetic transition near 78 K, close to the experimental $T_{\mathrm{C}}$. Concurrently, magnetic reconstruction profoundly reshapes the reciprocal-space topology, increasing the number of Weyl-point pairs from 42 in the collinear ferromagnetic state to 115 in the non-coplanar state. Berry-curvature calculations yield an intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity of $\sim983$ S cm$^{-1}$ at the experimentally determined carrier concentration, closely reproducing the experimental intrinsic contribution of $\sim990$ S cm$^{-1}$. These results establish Nd$_4$Sb$_3$ as a compelling platform where magnetic reconstruction intertwines real-space spin chirality with momentum-space Weyl topology.

Topological Materials.title: Field-selected seven-site topological magnons in a classical frustrated triangular-lattice K - Γ - Γ ’magnet
Topological Materials.authors: Bin Xi, Jie Lu, Shun-Li Yu, Yafang Xu
Topological Materials.abstract: Defining magnon topology in strongly frustrated magnets is often hindered by the absence of a simple harmonic magnon vacuum at zero field. Within a classical-spin ground-state search followed by linear spin-wave theory (LSWT), we demonstrate that a representative triangular-lattice K-Gamma-Gamma' model in a dominant-Gamma exchange regime has an in-plane-field-selected compact, noncoplanar seven-site order. This field-selected state provides a controlled classical reference state and hosts magnon bands with field-tunable Chern numbers. Increasing the field drives a Dirac-like band touching that transfers Berry curvature between the fifth and sixth bands, altering the Chern vector from (0, 1, 0, -2, 1, 0, 0) to (0, 1, 0, -2, -1, 2, 0). This topological transition reorganizes the band-resolved thermal Hall conductivity, driving the total $κ_{xy}(T)$ through a near-zero crossing once the upper bands are thermally populated. The dynamical structure factor places roughly half of the coherent spectral weight on the Chern-active branches, offering a spectroscopic route to identify the topological branches. These results define a controlled semiclassical benchmark for magnon topology in this pure nearest-neighbor exchange model.

Topological Materials.title: Molecular-orbital origin of weak orbital ferromagnetism and anomalous Hall effect in a trimerized kagome antiferromagnet
Topological Materials.authors: I. V. Solovyev
Topological Materials.abstract: We reveal the molecular-orbital origin of weak orbital ferromagnetism and the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) induced by noncollinear spin order in a trimerized kagome lattice. By transforming to the molecular-orbital basis of an isolated trimer in the double-exchange regime, we derive an effective low-energy model for the states with opposite orbital angular momenta $m= \pm 1$ subject to an effective Zeeman field arising from spin chirality and spin-orbit (SO) coupling. In this representation, the kagome-lattice problem maps onto a triangular lattice of trimers, while the nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor hoppings of the original lattice generate complex hopping amplitudes between neighboring trimers. This formulation provides a transparent picture of how spin chirality and SO coupling can be recast as an effective Zeeman field that lifts the degeneracy of the $m= \pm 1$ states, breaks time-reversal symmetry, and thereby gives rise to weak orbital ferromagnetism and the AHE. The resulting phase diagram includes metallic phases, topologically trivial insulating phases, as well as several topological phases characterized by nonzero Chern numbers and the quantum anomalous Hall effect. We further identify an alternative route to time-reversal-symmetry breaking and orbital magnetization, driven by an emergent gauge field arising solely from complex inter-trimer hoppings and requiring no effective Zeeman field.

Topological Materials.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
Topological Materials.authors: Narsimha Rao Elaprolu, Marco Gibertini
Topological Materials.abstract: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. First-principles calculations for bilayer CrSBr illustrate this mechanism within a compressed orthorhombic structural model. Out-of-plane magnetization yields a Chern insulator with a chiral edge state, whereas in-plane magnetization supports a two-dimensional Weyl semimetal with node-connecting edge states. Continuous spin canting further demonstrates how magnetic reorientation can drive the transition and stabilize the Chern phase before full magnetic saturation. Although material-specific transition conditions depend on electronic correlations and structural stability under compression, the underlying strategy identifies interlayer hybridization as a link between magnetic order and band topology. These results provide a design principle for externally tunable topological phases in layered antiferromagnetic semiconductors.

Topological Materials.title: Fermi-level tuning and electron correlation effects on the anomalous Nernst response in Ni-substituted Co 2 MnGa
Topological Materials.authors: Benugopal Bairagya, Guangzong Xing, Nanhe Kumar Gupta, Weinan Zhou, Kodchakorn Simalaotao, Keisuke Masuda, Sanjay Singh, Yuya Sakuraba
Topological Materials.abstract: The anomalous Nernst effect (ANE) in magnetic topological materials originates from Berry curvature near the Fermi energy and generates a transverse thermoelectric voltage perpendicular to the applied thermal gradient. The Heusler compound Co2MnGa, a Weyl semimetal with the L21 structure, exhibits a large anomalous Hall effect and an anomalous Nernst response among the largest reported at room temperature. Theoretical calculations predict that the maximum anomalous Nernst conductivity (αxy[A]) lies slightly above the Fermi energy, thereby motivating electron doping as a route to enhance the ANE response. To examine this, Ni substitution at the Co site was employed to tune the Fermi energy while retaining the ordered structure. Although a clear Fermi-level shift was experimentally confirmed, no enhancement in αxy[A] was observed. The discrepancy with theory is reconciled by incorporating on-site Coulomb interactions for the Co-3d states, which restores consistency between calculation and experiment and highlights the critical role of electron correlation in Co-based Heusler systems.

Topological Materials.title: Probing the Dirac Quantum Geometry in Quantum Magnets from Polarized Raman Spectroscopy
Topological Materials.authors: Yuki Yamazaki, Doh Young Kim, Takahiro Morimoto, Bohm-Jung Yang
Topological Materials.abstract: Magnetic Raman spectroscopy is sensitive to quasiparticle quantum geometry, yet microscopic Raman vertices generally prevent a direct geometric interpretation. Here we establish a symmetry-based extraction principle for two-dimensional quantum magnets with two-band quasiparticle excitations. Opposite circular-polarization spectra separate vertex-weighted quantum-metric and Berry-curvature contractions. Near a $C_3$-symmetric massive Dirac valley, symmetry fixes the leading Raman and velocity doublets up to a common scale, allowing the unknown Raman strength and intensity normalization to cancel from their spectral ratio. For an inversion-related pair of massive Dirac cones, the normalized counter-circular Raman asymmetry at frequency threshold $Ω_{\rm th}$ is fixed by the Chern number and follows a universal near-threshold frequency scaling. This yields a local spectroscopic readout without absolute-intensity calibration or frequency integration. We demonstrate the principle for Majorana fermions in the field-induced honeycomb Kitaev spin liquid and for topological magnons in a honeycomb ferromagnet, and identify the conditions for resolving it experimentally.

Topological Materials.title: Valley-polarized quantum anomalous hall effect in alkali metal-doped VI 3 monolayers
Topological Materials.authors: Wenlu Zhang, Xiaoxiao Man, Yajie Zheng, Yaling Zhang, Jie Xu, Liang Gu, Yongli Xie, Xiaoqing Gao, Xiaoyu Cheng, Junhua Hou, Meize Li, Huisheng Zhang, Xiaohong Xu
Topological Materials.abstract: Valley-polarized quantum anomalous Hall effect (VP-QAHE), which combines dissipationless chiral edge states and valley polarization in one system, holds promising applications for the development of low-dissipation valleytronic devices. However, realizing such an intriguing quantum phenomenon in real materials remains a significant challenge. Here, we propose alkali metal doping as an effective strategy to realize VP-QAHE in the two-dimensional (2D) ferromagnetic VI3 monolayer. Based on first-principles calculations, we find that the VI3 monolayer undergoes the semiconducting to half-metallic phase transition upon alkali-metal doping, which also significantly increases its Curie temperature from 41 K to 210 K for Na doping. Most importantly, it is found that Na- and strained Li-doped VI3 harbor VP-QAHE due to the synergy of Jahn-Teller distortion and spin-orbit coupling. This work provides a feasible material design route for the exploration of valley-polarized topological states in the 2D regime, benefiting practical applications in valleytronics.

Topological Materials.title: Reversal of the Anomalous Hall Effect by Directional In-Plane Electric Field in Strained Bilayer MoO
Topological Materials.authors: Wenpeng Wang, hang Shi, Xiangru Kong
Topological Materials.abstract: Layered magnetic materials with tunable valley and spin degrees of freedom hold promise for multifunctional spintronic devices. Here, we demonstrate that the orientation of an in-plane electric field enables selective switching of single-valley spin splitting and reversal of the anomalous Hall conductivity in strained bilayer MoO. In particular, electric fields along the a and b directions selectively lift the spin degeneracy at the X and Y valleys, respectively, while preserving it at the other valley. This valley-selective switching is accompanied by a redistribution of Berry curvature with opposite signs, giving rise to a reversible anomalous Hall response. These effects are realized in the energetically and dynamically stable AC2 stacking configuration, where biaxial strain induces Dirac-like band crossings that enable subsequent electric-field control. Meanwhile, the AC1 stacking configuration, which is also energetically and dynamically stable, exhibits rich strain-driven phenomena, including a transition from metal to topological insulator with quantized spin Hall conductivity, as well as valley polarization and piezomagnetism. Our findings reveal a combined effect of strain and electric fields for controlling valley-selective spin splitting and anomalous Hall responses, highlighting bilayer MoO as a promising platform for multifunctional spintronic and valleytronic devices.

Topological Materials.title: MagBerry: A Julia package for modeling magnon and phonon topology and transport
Topological Materials.authors: Xiaonong Shen, Wei Ren
Topological Materials.abstract: We present MagBerry, a Julia package for studying the topology and transport of magnons, phonons, and their hybrid excitations. It combines magnetic models and linear spin-wave Hamiltonians from Sunny.jl with native modules for harmonic phonons and magnon--phonon coupling. These excitations are treated within a common bosonic Bogoliubov--de Gennes formulation. The package calculates bulk and boundary spectra, Berry curvature, and Chern numbers, and resolves the spin and phonon angular momentum carried by each mode. Transport calculations include thermal Hall, spin and orbital Nernst, and phonon angular momentum Hall responses. The package also evaluates the extended Berry curvature dipole contribution to nonlinear magnon thermal Hall transport. Relaxation-time Boltzmann theory gives heat and angular momentum currents. Examples based on published models reproduce topological magnon boundary spectra and illustrate phonon geometry and nonlinear transport. For an altermagnetic hybrid model, we extend a published study of the d-wave phonon angular momentum texture by calculating its Boltzmann transport coefficients. The resulting tensor describes how the longitudinal and transverse angular momentum currents vary with temperature and the direction of the temperature gradient.

Topological Materials.title: Theory of anisotropic magnetotransport beyond the constant relaxation-time approximation in multi-Weyl semimetals
Topological Materials.authors: Azaz Ahmad, Shantanu Mukherjee, Mohd Hashim Raza, Gautham Varma K., Takami Tohyama
Topological Materials.abstract: Multi-Weyl semimetals, characterized by Weyl nodes carrying higher monopole charges, provide a platform for exploring topological magnetotransport beyond the conventional Weyl paradigm. Here, we develop a generalized semiclassical Boltzmann framework for multi-Weyl semimetals with arbitrary monopole charge $N$, incorporating the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) into the quasiparticle dispersion and Berry-curvature-modified dynamics, together with a momentum-dependent collision integral accounting for intra- and intervalley scattering. We investigate the longitudinal magnetoconductivity (LMC) and planar Hall conductivity (PHC) for $N=1$, $2$, and $3$, considering both nonmagnetic and magnetic impurity scattering. In the absence of OMM, the LMC remains positive and quadratic in the magnetic field throughout the investigated scattering regime, consistent with conventional chiral-anomaly-assisted transport. Including OMM, however, leads to a sign reversal of the LMC under sufficiently strong intervalley scattering for the $σ_0$ and $σ_z$ impurity channels. Remarkably, the critical intervalley scattering strength decreases systematically with increasing monopole charge, indicating an enhanced tendency toward negative LMC in higher-charge Weyl systems. Furthermore, we find that the PHC also undergoes a sign reversal for $N=2$ and $N=3$ in the same impurity channels, while remaining positive for $N=1$ within the investigated parameter range. The angular dependences retain their characteristic $\sin^2γ$-like and $\sin2γ$ profiles for LMC and PHC, respectively, even across the sign reversal. Our results demonstrate that the interplay of Berry curvature, OMM, monopole charge, and impurity scattering can produce qualitatively distinct weak-field magnetotransport responses beyond the conventional chiral-anomaly picture.

Topological Materials.title: Magnetic-Field-Tuned Critical End Point and High-Field Phases in HoMn6Sn6
Topological Materials.authors: Joanna Blawat, John Singleton, Junho Seo, Charles Mielke, Tyler J. Slade, Paul C. Canfield, Philip J. W. Moll, Ross D. McDonald, Robert J. McQueeney
Topological Materials.abstract: Topological Kagome RMn6Sn6 materials, where R is a rare-earth, exhibit a rich variety of magnetic phases which provide an opportunity to understand how different spin textures affect topological and transport properties through the application of magnetic field H. In this work, we report experiments on single-crystal HoMn6Sn6, made possible by pulsed magnetic fields of up to 60 T, that permit high-field features of the field-temperature phase diagram to be studied in detail using magnetometry. Complementary, sensitive transport experiments over the same field range employ focused-ion-beam fabrication of novel strain-relieved HoMn6Sn6 devices. In agreement with meanfield calculations, we find a metamagnetic transition at 45 T with H||c between canted phases that ends in a critical end point at about 90 K. As far as we are aware, this is the only critical endpoint that is observed within the RMn6Sn6 kagome metals, and its temperature and field far exceed those of analogous phenomena in other materials. In the low-temperature metamagnetic region, HoMn6Sn6 shows large magnetoresistance, reaching 900 % at 60 T, in concert with Shubnikov de Haas oscillations that suggest a slight Fermi-surface contraction as the metamagnetic transition is crossed. A phase analysis of the oscillations suggests non-trivial band topology, although a firmer attribution must await detailed bandstructure calculations. Near the critical end point, we find deviations from Fermi-liquid behavior in the temperature-dependent magnetoresistance. In the metamagnetic region, the anomalous Hall contribution is not proportional to magnetization, and peaks at about 40 K, suggesting the role of enhanced spin fluctuations near the critical point. At higher temperatures, the anomalous Hall effect reappears at low fields, showing that the magnetization provided by the Ho and Mn sublattices independently affect the conductivity.

Topological Materials.title: Unconventional excitations and orbital-driven low-energy dispersions in the chiral topological semimetals PdAsS, PdSbSe, and PdBiTe: A first-principles study
Topological Materials.authors: Roopam Pandey, Sudhir K. Pandey
Topological Materials.abstract: The appearance of higher-fold excitations are typically governed by space group symmetry. However, physical factors affecting local structural and electronic environment such as atomic arrangement, orbital overlaps, etc., largely alter the behavior of quasiparticle around higher-fold nodes. In this work, we consider three chiral material candidates (space group P21 3) which exhibit systematic variations in physical parameters by virtue of their constituent elements. We perform a detailed and systematic study of these materials using density functional theory (DFT) in absence and presence of spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Four different kinds of unconventional excitations were observed in all three materials at Γ- and R-point in the full BZ. In absence of SOC, we find spin-1 (Γ) and double Weyl (R) excitations, whereas a Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl fermion (Γ) and double spin-1 excitation (R) are found in presence of SOC. All of these higher fold nodes lie in energy range of (−0.5, −0.85) eV. Remarkably, we also find total of eight new type-II Weyl points even in absence of SOC on Γ-R line in these materials. In presence of SOC, 24 new Weyl nodes of type-I/II nature at general are also observed. The presence of these Weyl nodes have not been reported momenta (kx , ky , kz ) 2π/a in any of the earlier works. Further, analyzing the low-energy dispersion of spin-1 excitations in these materials, we find that otherwise flat middle band in PdBiTe is almost parabolic due strong hybridization. On the other hand, relatively flat middle bands can be observed in PdAsS and PdSbSe in low-energy scale. In case of double spin-1 excitations, surprisingly, we see linearly dispersing middle bands in PdSbSe whereas middle bands in PdAsS and PdBiTe are parabolic even in low-energy scale. We believe our results provide essential insights for realizing and designing topological materials for emerging quantum applications. Lastly, we present non-trivial surface states and Fermi arcs associated with higher fold excitations.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Optical spin Edelstein response of d-wave altermagnets
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: M. A. Mojarro, R. Carrillo-Bastos, Jesús A. Maytorena
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: The momentum-dependent spin splitting and compensated magnetic order in altermagnets offer opportunities for electrical control of spin polarization. We explore the spin Edelstein effect in the frequency domain of a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnet with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. We calculate the spin-velocity susceptibility response function beyond the intraband response regime and find that the interband longitudinal and transverse Edelstein responses are governed by the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature, respectively. The density of states presents a logarithmic van Hove singularity at exactly the negative value of the energy below which four disconnected Fermi contours emerge. This defines three distinctive regions for the position of the Fermi level, through which the Edelstein susceptibility tensor displays characteristic spectral features, reflecting the topological change of the Fermi surface. The resulting spin magnetization shows a strong dependence on the driving frequency and on the orientation of the in-plane external electric field. Our results highlight new possibilities for electrical and optical control of the spin Edelstein effect in altermagnets that could find spintronic applications.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Altermagnetism-induced magneto-optical effects
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Jun Ōiké, Robert Peters, Koki Shinada
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Altermagnets break time-reversal symmetry despite their zero net magnetization, enabling time-reversal-odd responses while retaining the advantages of antiferromagnets. However, magneto-optical (MO) effects are not universal among altermagnets because MO effects typically arise from magnetic dipole order (ferromagnetism), which is generally absent in altermagnets. In this work, we address this limitation by establishing octupolar MO effects, which arise from magnetic octupole order through spatial dispersion. Owing to this distinct origin, octupolar MO effects do not necessarily require spin-orbit coupling even in collinear magnets and can arise without an external magnetic field in antiferromagnets where conventional MO effects are symmetry-forbidden. Such antiferromagnets include $d$-wave altermagnets such as RuO$_2$ and KV$_2$Se$_2$O, certain $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, including CrSb, as well as noncoplanar antiferromagnets such as MnTe$_2$ and pyrochlore iridates with all-in-all-out magnetic order. From an experimental perspective, octupolar MO effects can reach detectable magnitudes and offer potential for magnetic-domain imaging, as supported by numerical calculations showing $μ$rad-scale Faraday rotation for a 100-nm-thick sample in the visible-light range and a sign reversal between opposite domains. Furthermore, octupolar MO effects are linked to an $f$-sum rule, enabling a quantitative estimate of the spin magnetic octupole moment from optical measurements. These results extend the scope of MO effects to a broad class of antiferromagnets, including altermagnets, and open a field-free optical route to exploring magnetic octupole order.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Altermagnetism in moiré quasicrystals
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Zi-Ming Wang, Rui Chen, Dong-Hui Xu
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Altermagnetism is a collinear compensated magnetic phase with zero net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin polarization. Quasicrystalline altermagnetism extends altermagnetism beyond periodic crystals, with noncrystallographic symmetries allowing high-order spin polarization patterns. Here, we propose a symmetry-based approach to realizing quasicrystalline altermagnetism by twisting collinear magnetic layers. Specifically, we demonstrate that the $30^{\circ}$-twisted honeycomb lattice bilayers form the dodecagonal quasicrystals supporting an $i$-wave altermagnetic phase. We further find that $45^{\circ}$-twisted bilayers preserving fourfold rotational symmetry support a mirror-driven $l$-wave phase with eight nodal lines. We characterize these altermagnetic patterns through plane-wave-projected spin-resolved spectral functions and spin-resolved conductances. Our work provides a systematic route to high-angular-order quasicrystalline altermagnetism through twist engineering.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Higher-order topology induced by altermagnetism in quasicrystals
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Xingmin Huo, Xingchuan Zhu, Xingyu Ma, Shiping Feng, Huaiming Guo
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Altermagnetism (AM), a novel magnetic phase featuring zero net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin splitting, provides a compelling platform for exploring exotic quantum phenomena. While recent studies have extended the concept of AM to quasicrystals, the momentum-dependent spin splitting in the absence of translational symmetry remains inadequately understood. Here, we investigate the emergence of higher-order topological phases (HOTPs) in Thue-Morse and Ammann-Beenker quasicrystals, driven by the coupling between d -wave quasicrystal AM orders and a two-dimensional topological insulator. We reveal that the d x 2 − y 2 -wave AM exhibits a ferromagnetism-like aspect in opening edge gaps and inducing zero-energy higher-order topological corner states. In contrast, conventional antiferromagnetic and d x y -wave AM configurations are unable to induce the higher-order topological gaps. These findings highlight the pivotal role of altermagnetic symmetry and its alignment with lattice corners in the realization of HOTPs and establish that the emergence of HOTPs can serve as a signature for identifying altermagnetic orders in aperiodic systems.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Sliding ferroelectricity and altermagnetic spin splitting in multilayer VPSe 3
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Yuchen Li, Xumin Chen, Shuisheng Yi, Peng Han, Jie Wang, Dexuan Huo, Rui Xiong
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Two-dimensional $\mathrm{MP}{\mathrm{X}}_{3}$ ($\mathrm{M}=\mathrm{Mn}$, V; $\mathrm{X}=\mathrm{S}$, Se) monolayers are van der Waals (vdW) antiferromagnets protected by inversion $\overline{E}$ symmetry. In multilayer $\mathrm{MP}{\mathrm{X}}_{3}$, interlayer sliding breaks inversion $\overline{E}$ symmetry to generate sliding ferroelectricity while preserving the rotational $C$ or mirror $M$ symmetry relating the opposite-spin sublattices. Consequently, interlayer sliding also drives the transition from antiferromagnetism to altermagnetism. Here, we systematically investigate the tunable sliding ferroelectricity and altermagnetism in multilayer $\mathrm{VPS}{\mathrm{e}}_{3}$ based on first principles. We demonstrate that interlayer sliding induces charge redistribution and robust out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization with a switching barrier of approximately 50 meV/u.c.. The ferroelectric polarization increases from 0.14 pC/m in the bilayer to 0.54 pC/m in the tetralayer, through cooperative accumulation of interfacial charge transfer across multiple interfaces. Sliding ferroelectricity switches altermagnetic spin polarization in bilayer $\mathrm{VPS}{\mathrm{e}}_{3}$. Furthermore, trilayer $\mathrm{VPS}{\mathrm{e}}_{3}$ introduces an intermediate antiferromagnetic state, enabling reversible switching between altermagnetic and antiferromagnetic phases beyond conventional binary spin switching. Tetralayer $\mathrm{VPS}{\mathrm{e}}_{3}$ generates multiple polarization states with distinct spin-splitting magnitudes, realizing multistate control of altermagnetic properties. The spin splitting increases from approximately 16 meV in the bilayer to approximately 23 meV in the tetralayer. This work establishes a direct connection between sliding ferroelectricity and altermagnetism in multilayer system, demonstrating layer engineering as an effective strategy for tuning altermagnetic spin splitting. These findings provide new insights into the interplay between ferroelectricity and altermagnetism and open opportunities for low-power electrically controllable spintronic devices.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Fractional quantum ferroelectric control of spin-valley locking and valley Hall effects in altermagnetic monolayer Cr 2 S 2
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Tao Yao, Quan Shen, Jiansheng Dong, Jianing Tan
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Fractional quantum multiferroics, arising from the coupling between fractional quantum ferroelectricity (FQFE) and altermagnetism (AM), provide a promising platform for nonvolatile control of momentum dependent spin splitting in systems with zero net magnetization. However, extending this FQFE-AM coupling to valley degrees of freedom and Berry curvature driven valley Hall effects remains largely unexplored. Here, using first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that monolayer Cr2S2 realizes a two dimensional FQFE-AM platform with two switchable FQFE states connected by composite symmetry operations combining a fractional lattice translation with time reversal or parity-time reversal. We show that FQFE switching reverses the AM spin-polarized band structure and interchanges the spin characters of the X and Y valleys without rotating the Néel vector, thereby enabling polarization switchable spin-valley locking. Moreover, the two FQFE states exhibit reversed Berry curvature distributions, which, together with the switched spin-valley locking, enable polarization controlled valley Hall effects under both electron and hole doping. These results demonstrate a symmetry based mechanism for nonvolatile electrical control of AM spin splitting, spin-valley locking, and valley Hall effects, offering a general route toward low-power valleytronic devices based on FQFE-AM coupling.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Evidence for hidden altermagnetism in Cs 1 − δ V 2 Te 2 O
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Guowei Yang, Ruihan Chen, Changchao Liu, Jing Li, Teng Hua, Ze Pan, Pengyue Xiong, Liwei Deng, Naifu Zheng, Shuntianjiao Ling, Yu Tang, Hao Zheng, Weifan Zhu, Yifu Xu, Xin Ma, Xiaoping Wang, Shengtao Cui, Zhe Sun, Zhengtai Liu, Mao Ye, Chao Cao, Ming Shi, Lunhui Hu, Qihang Liu, Shan Qiao, Guanghan Cao, Yu Song, Yang Liu
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Altermagnets are characterized by anisotropic band/spin splittings in momentum space, dictated by their spin-space group symmetries. However, the real-space modulations of altermagnetism are often neglected and have not been explored experimentally. Here we combine neutron diffraction, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), spin-resolved ARPES and density functional theory to demonstrate that Cs$_{1-δ}$V$_2$Te$_2$O realizes a spatially modulated form of altermagnetism, i.e., hidden altermagnetism. Such a state in Cs$_{1-δ}$V$_2$Te$_2$O results from its G-type antiferromagnetism and two-dimensional electronic states, allowing for the development of spatially alternating altermagnetic layers, whose local spin polarizations are directly verified by spin-resolved ARPES measurements. Our experimental discovery of hidden altermagnetism broadens the scope of unconventional magnetism and opens routes to exploring emergent phenomena from real-space modulations of altermagnetic order.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Nonlocal multipolar spin accumulation in altermagnets beyond d-wave
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: J. W. Gonzalez
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: In spin-conserving models of $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, the uniform longitudinal conductivity has no spin-odd component. A point injector reveals higher moments of the Fermi velocity through the nonlocal spin accumulation. Boltzmann theory predicts that the rank $m=2,4,6$ of the first nonzero spin-odd velocity moment sets the leading angular harmonic, its asymptotic radial dependence $r^{2-m}$, and its amplitude scaling $τ^{m-3}$ at fixed distance and injected current. For $g$-wave order, the fourth moment produces a fourth angular harmonic with an asymptotic $r^{-2}$ tail. Quantum transport simulations support the radial profiles predicted by finite-geometry Boltzmann theory without an amplitude fit. Across the three symmetries, the quantum amplitudes exceed the Boltzmann predictions based on the Born scattering time by $15-65$\% in the windows analyzed. In a two-contact ribbon, we detect the $g$-wave fourth harmonic at $6.8\,σ$ in an independent set of 1800 disorder realizations using a preselected radial window. Its amplitude decreases when the altermagnetic splitting is reduced.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Disentangling Spin and Orbital Contributions in the Search for Altermagnetic Terahertz Conversion in RuO2
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Jiahao Liu, Yuxiao Mo, Tongyang Guan, Wenhui Fang, Yongwei Cui, Wentao Qin, Zhe Yuan, Lishu Zhang, Zhensheng Tao, Yizheng Wu
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Rutile RuO2 has emerged as a prominent candidate altermagnet, yet the microscopic origin of its reported charge-angular-momentum conversion remains unsettled. Recent theoretical and experimental advances have highlighted a potentially dominant role of orbital transport, raising a fundamental ambiguity between spin- and orbital-mediated conversion in RuO2. Here, we report the first experimental disentanglement of the spin- and orbital-to-charge conversion channels in RuO2 heterostructures using terahertz emission spectroscopy. We identify Fe as a predominantly spin-current injector, whereas Ni and permalloy predominantly inject orbital currents, revealing a substantial orbital contribution to ultrafast terahertz emission. Under controlled spin-current injection, we find no evidence for inverse altermagnetic spin-splitting effect. Instead, the observed anisotropy is consistent with an anisotropic inverse spin Hall response that is strongly conditioned by the near-interface environment. Under orbital-current injection, the anisotropy is markedly weaker, indicating that orbital-to-charge conversion is largely isotropic in RuO2. Our results establish orbital transport and interface-conditioned spin Hall conversion as key to terahertz emission from RuO2, underscoring the need to disentangle spin, orbital, and interfacial contributions before assigning anisotropy to altermagnetism.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Bichromatic light-induced electronic torques on the Néel vector in Rashba magnetic multipoles from $p$-wave magnets to $i$-wave altermagnets
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Mohsen Yarmohammadi
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Light can control magnetic order on ultrafast timescales, but for a two-dimensional magnet with an out-of-plane order parameter $\boldsymbol N\parallel\hat z$, the inverse Faraday field is collinear with $\boldsymbol N$ and gives no transverse torque. Here we show that bichromatic $(ω,bω)$ light generates electronic torques perpendicular to $\boldsymbol N$ in Rashba-coupled magnetic multipoles, from $p$-wave ($n=1$) magnets to $i$-wave ($n=6$) altermagnets. Beyond high-frequency effective fields, we evaluate the exact Floquet response and the generalized torque per occupied electron, for prescribed occupations. The momentum-dependent exchange terms dominate this Fermi-sea torque and remove the leading-order zeros (amplitude-ratio blindspots) of the momentum-independent field in the channels tested. For out-of-plane $\boldsymbol N$, rotational symmetry permits a transverse torque only if $\gcd(n,b+1)=1$ for counter-rotating beams or $\gcd(n,b-1)=1$ for co-rotating beams. For in-plane $\boldsymbol N$, the Fermi sea also gives a torque component along $\hat z$ that the momentum-independent field cannot produce. We classify the active channels, with $n=1,\dots,6$ and $b=1,\dots,7$, by frequency scaling and origin (cycle-averaged versus oscillating exchange). As a control, a Rashba ferromagnet ($n=0$) has one symmetry-allowed out-of-plane channel and a weak in-plane response without a selection rule. Finite-momentum occupied-state physics is therefore essential for light-driven torques in unconventional magnets, and the exact Floquet calculation validates and extends the high-frequency description.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Altermagnetic materials library in intercalated transition-metal dichalcogenides
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Ezra Day-Roberts, Huan Wu, Onur Erten, Antia S. Botana
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Altermagnets represent a promising class of magnetic materials owing to their distinctive spin-split band structures in the absence of net magnetization. Here, we present a first-principles investigation of altermagnetism in magnetically intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) with the general formula T y MX 2 (T= 3d-transition metal, M= transition-metal, X=chalcogen, y= 1/4 or 1/3). For a TMD host with 2H structure, compounds exhibiting A-type antiferromagnetism are g-wave altermagnets by symmetry for both y= 1/4 and 1/3. We identify several intercalated TMDs fulfilling the conditions for altermagnetic order to be realized. Several of these candidate materials display spin-splittings at the Fermi level as large as 100 meV.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Narrow-Band Magnetism Allowed by Quantum Geometry: Altermagnetism and Beyond
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Minxuan Wang, Pei-Han Lin, Yang Ge, Jiabin Yu
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Quantum geometry plays a central role in shaping correlated phases in narrow bands, yet its influence on the competition between distinct magnetic orders, especially the emergence of altermagnetism, remains largely unexplored. To address this question, we study the quadrupole insulator model with strictly onsite generalized Hubbard-Kanamori interactions, in which both Néel antiferromagnetism and altermagnetism are symmetry-permitted. Depending on the parameters, the isolated narrow lowest band of the model can either be obstructed atomic with strong quantum geometry or trivial atomic with weak quantum geometry, while the dispersion is identical in the two cases. By partially filling the lowest band, our Hartree-Fock calculations show only conventional ferromagnetic phases for the weak quantum geometric case, while we find two collinear altermagnetic phases, as well as nematic phases, for the strong quantum geometric case. Such a dramatic difference can be understood by the distinct characters of the projected interaction: the projected interactions acquire sizable longer-range channels only for the strong quantum geometric case, while they are dominated by the on-site Hubbard channel in the weak quantum geometric case. These results establish the essential role of quantum geometry for altermagnetism to emerge from interacting narrow bands where crystalline symmetries cannot sufficiently constrain the magnetic order.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Probing Chern Topology through Hall-Sensitive Photonic Spin Hall Shifts in a d-wave Altermagnet
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Mahnoor Sajid, Maha Siddiqui, Muzamil Shah
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the photonic spin Hall effect in a two-dimensional Rashba-coupled $d$-wave altermagnetic Chern system subjected to a uniform out-of-plane exchange field. We first analyze the energy-band structure and the Dirac mass distribution at the high-symmetry points, where $m_Γ=m_M=Δ_x, m_X=Δ_x-4 t_J$, and $m_Y=Δ_x+4 t_J$. Band inversions at high-symmetry points generate both a topologically trivial regime $(C=0)$ and Chern-insulating phases $(C= \pm 1)$. Employing the Kubo formalism for the optical conductivity together with the reflection matrix for a substrate-supported conducting sheet, we compute helicity-dependent finite-waist displacements of a reflected Gaussian beam. The resulting optical response exhibits a minimum interband absorption threshold, a Van Hove-type spectral feature, and distinct transitions at the $X$ and $Y$ points arising from the momentum dependence of the exchange field. Under the specified Hall-tensor and polarization sign conventions, the longitudinal helicity half-separation is odd upon reversal of the optical Hall conductivity and correspondingly changes sign between opposite-Chern phases, whereas the transverse half-separation is even in the Hall response. The maximal spin-dependent splitting occur in the vicinity of the pseudo-Brewster reflectance minimum. The longitudinal spin splitting reverses sign between opposite Chern phases, reflecting the exchange-controlled optical Hall response, while its pronounced spectral variations reveal the influence of inequivalent interband transitions induced by the $d$-wave altermagnetic exchange. These findings establish polarization-resolved photonic beam shifts as a sensitive probe of Hall-active topological phases and their characteristic optical spectra.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Tunneling magnetoresistance effect in an altermagnet/insulator/ferromagnet junction
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Yu-Fei Sun, Yue Mao, Yu-Chen Zhuang, Tian-Yi Zhang, Qing-Feng Sun

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in 𝒫 𝒯 antiferromagnets
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: K. D. Belashchenko
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Surface altermagnetism extends spin splitting beyond bulk altermagnets through symmetry reduction at surfaces and interfaces. An existing classification applies to the local symmetry of atomically flat surface terraces. Here we address the symmetry of macroscopic spin-momentum correlations that survive averaging over compensated rough surfaces. These correlations are governed by the surface antisymmetry Laue class. Because rough-surface altermagnetism is forbidden at any surface of a magnet with antitranslations, the classification reduces to P T -symmetric antiferromagnets. By restoring all symmetries leaving the surface normal invariant, roughness can generate compensated surface altermagnets from uncompensated flat terminations or suppress spin splitting. Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in P T -symmetric antiferromagnets offers a route to combine bulk electrical switchability with altermagnetic surface transport.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Xuetao Ma, Zhaoyu Liu, Jiaqi Cai, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaodong Xu, Jiun-Haw Chu, Matthew Yankowitz
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Strongly correlated and topological phases in moiré materials are exquisitely sensitive to lattice geometry at both atomic and superlattice length scales. Twist angle, pressure, and strain directly modify the lattice and thus act as highly effective tuning parameters. Here, we examined electrical transport in twisted bilayer graphene subjected to continuous uniaxial strain. Near the magic angle (≈1.1°), devices exhibited a pronounced elastoresistance that depended on band filling and temperature, with a gauge factor more than two orders of magnitude larger than that of conventional metals. In selected doping regimes, the elastoresistance exhibited a Curie-Weiss–like temperature divergence. We discuss possible microscopic origins, including nematic fluctuations and enhanced electronic entropy from fluctuating isospin moments. Our work establishes uniaxial strain as a versatile probe of correlated physics in a moiré material.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Jiang Yuhan, Matthew Otten
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by fixed-point search and measured. One framework covers many targets, from formation energy and band gaps to elasticity and conductivity. We design the algorithm for the mature fault-tolerant era and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth from a classically routine benchmark to targets where established methods are unreliable. The approach generates candidate materials from first principles, rather than generalizing from those known, and could enable materials discovery when the target properties are difficult to predict classically.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Quartet ferromagnetism in the small-exchange limit
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Samuel Ogundeji, Tianxiong Han, Tyler J. Slade, Olivia Medina, Joanna M. Blawat, Filip Ronning, John Singleton, Sean M. Thomas, Alimamy F. Bangura, Wei Tian, Eleanor M. Clements, Bing Li, Adam A. Aczel, Paul C. Canfield, Benjamin G. Ueland, Rebecca Flint, Robert J. McQueeney, Aashish Sapkota
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Rare-earth magnets are often regarded as classical owing to their large angular momentum J, but this picture breaks down when exchange is smaller than the crystalline electric-field (CEF) energy scale, allowing the degeneracy of low-lying CEF manifolds to dictate the emergent quantum phases. Here, we uncover such a regime in the RV6Sn6 (R = rare-earth) kagome metals with strong magnetic anisotropy. Thermodynamic and neutron-diffraction measurements reveal successive axial and tilted ferromagnetic (FM) phases in DyV6Sn6, arising from independent ordering of the axial Mz and transverse Mx dipolar components enabled by a rare quasi-quartet ground state. On the other hand, HoV6Sn6 has a similar tilted magnetic anisotropy, but remains axial down to 0.03 K. This discrepancy can be traced back to the non-Kramers nature of Ho3+ where the CEF lifts the quartet degeneracy, leaving a quasi-triplet ground state. Unlike quartets or higher multiplets, we find that the effective spin-1 triplet does not allow independent dipolar ordering without strong quadrupolar (nematic) interactions that act to break rotational symmetry, revealing an essential multipolar prerequisite for tilted magnetic ground states. These results establish a quartet CEF manifold as the minimal degeneracy required for dipolar-driven independent ordering. Mapping the surrounding CEF parameter space further reveals competing magnetic, non-magnetic singlet, and potential quadrupolar phases, driven by multifold ground state degeneracies. These results establish CEF tuning as a versatile route to unconventional quantum phases across the broader RT6X6 (T = transition metal; X = Sn, Ge) family.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Spin Josephson supercurrent in altermagnetic superconducting nanowire junctions
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Yue Mao, Xing-Jian Yi, Yu-Chen Zhuang, Cheng-Ming Miao, Qing-Feng Sun
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: The spin supercurrent is a key concept for enabling energy-efficient operation. In this Letter, we propose that a spin Josephson supercurrent can be generated in altermagnetic superconducting nanowire (SNW) junctions. We present a physical picture in which a superconducting gap with a dominant spin-triplet component can be induced in an altermagnetic SNW. Using the nonequilibrium Green’s function method, we systematically investigate the spin Josephson supercurrent in an altermagnetic SNW/normal metal/altermagnetic SNW junction. We demonstrate that both the superconducting phase difference and spin phase difference can drive the spin Josephson supercurrent, and we also analyze the symmetries underlying the current-phase relations. Furthermore, the results reveal a spin superconducting diode effect, characterized by nonreciprocal critical spin supercurrents. This work provides new perspectives on generating spin supercurrents via altermagnets.

Novel Quantum Materials.title: Ultrafast Moiré Exciton Dynamics Revealed by Two-Dimensional Coherent Spectroscopy
Novel Quantum Materials.authors: Deran Zhang, Zhexue Chen, Dongxue Chen, Tengfei Yan, Jianhua Jiang, Hui Dong
Novel Quantum Materials.abstract: Moiré superlattices of van der Waals heterostructures confine excitons into discrete energy levels in finite-sized samples, yet their internal relaxation pathways remain obscured by inhomogeneous broadening. Here, using two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy (2DCS), we directly resolve seven discrete energy levels of the moiré-confined intralayer $\mathrm{WS}_{2}$ A exciton in an hBN-encapsulated $\mathrm{WS}_{2}/\mathrm{WSe}_{2}$ heterostructure, corresponding to a confinement depth of 57.02 meV. By tracking the population of these levels over picosecond delays, we uncover a two-stage thermalization process: an effective exciton temperature drops from 171.8 to 99.3 K within 1.2 ps through rapid intra-manifold population redistribution, followed by a slower recovery toward quasi-equilibrium mediated by exciton--environment interactions. Kullback--Leibler divergence analysis confirms the progressive transition from a non-equilibrium to a Boltzmann-distributed population. Our results establish state-resolved access to moiré exciton dynamics and provide a foundation for exploring nonequilibrium many-body phenomena in moiré quantum materials.
